Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Ms. Smith asked about the design of the tower. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and suggested that the applicant might be able to better address.

Mr. Jonathan Yates reviewed the request with the Commission (attachment 3).

Mr. Robert Hill, representative for T-mobile, explained the need for the cell tower. He showed a depiction of the locations of the current cell towers located near Rivertowne and the coverage for the area (attachment 3). He stated that they had several community meetings regarding this request.

Mr. Wren asked if there are existing locations where the tower could be located and if the clubhouse could be utilized. Mr. Hill answered that the height of the Planning Commission

building would not allow the coverage needed. Mr. Wren asked if the tower would only service Rivertowne. Mr. Hill answered that based on the height and the amount of foliage, the tower would provide service for approximately ½ mile to 1 mile from the tower.

Mr. Millet asked the proximity of residential to the proposed location. Mr. Hill showed the location of the residential and proximity on the map for the Commission. Mr. Millet asked about the coverage. Mr. Keith Powell, representative for Verizon, showed the proposed coverage to the Commission.

Mr. Yates stated that the tower would serve several different wireless communication companies. He stated that the tower would be a stealth pole with an equipment building.

Mr. Michael Robinson, Charleston Appraisal, stated that he conducted an analysis on the effects of the construction of a cell tower in Mount Pleasant to property values and provided this information for the Commission to review (attachment 4). He stated that based on his analysis there was no impact to property values.

Mr. Powell reviewed how the tower would be seen from different areas near the proposed location for the Commission.

Mr. Yates stated that they conducted a community survey and Mr. Will Freeland reviewed the findings with the Commission. Mr. Freeland stated that approximately 79% of those that responded to the survey were in favor of the proposed tower.

Mr. Hank Cardarelli, 1864 Great Hope Drive, expressed concern that the cell tower would negatively affect property values. He stated that the HOA has covenants and restrictions regarding cell towers.

Mr. Robert Newman, 1836 Delacourt Ave, stated that they currently have low coverage and is in favor of the tower.

Mr. Kent Provada, Palmetto Isle, suggested that the survey should not be considered as it did not include an opportunity to consider other locations or Planning Commission

alternatives. He suggested that the cell tower could be placed on other property along Highway 41 that would provide coverage.

Mr. Michael Baumrind, 1537 Red Drum Road, stated that he supports the proposal. He stated that he works from home and finds that cell service is low in the area. He stated that he supports the request to provide better coverage. He suggested that the younger generation highly considers cell coverage when considering purchasing a home. He suggested that the additional tower would better distribute the volume, which would provide better service for the entire area.

Ms. Nina Thomas, 1824 Palmetto Isle Drive, expressed concern for the potential radiation that the cell tower could emit and that it would cause health issues for children and residents in the surrounding area. She suggested that the tower is too close in proximity to residential neighborhoods and amenities. She suggested that the proposal is unacceptable and should not be approved.

Mr. Jeff Poplar, president of HOA of Pointe in North Creek and on the board of Parker’s Island HOA. He stated that wireless capability within neighborhoods is a necessity for home sales. He suggested that a majority of homes do not have landline phones and rely solely on cell service.

Ms. Kelly Wood, 1872 Great Hope Drive, stated that she is opposed to the request and agrees with the concerns of Ms. Thomas. She suggested that the proximity of the cell tower could increase the chances of cancer.

Mr. Joe Daily, member of Parkers Landing and Parkers Island boards, stated that the boards are in favor of the request. He stated that many homes no longer have land lines and rely on cell phones as their main telephone access. He suggested that not having good wireless service and coverage is also a safety issue as residents would possibly not be able to reach emergency personnel during emergency events. He asked that the request be approved.

Ms. Pam Fischette, 2528 Ballast Point, agrees that the proximity of the cell tower would increase the amount of radiation in the area. She suggested that other locations should be considered that would not be so close to residents. Planning Commission

Ms. Linda Woodfern, 1837 Palmetto Isle Drive, agreed that there is a safety issue with the location of the towers and agrees with Ms. Thomas’ comments. She agreed that a different location should be considered. She suggested that a booster can be provided from the different wireless carriers and suggested that this could be an alternative to constructing a new tower. She stated that she is opposed to the proposed location of the tower.

Ms. Sharon Salomon, 1844 Great Hope, stated that she is opposed to the location of the tower. She stated that there are a number of health concerns related to cell towers and radiation. She suggested that a different location should be considered.

Mr. Paul Cessna, 2791 Olympia Fields Lane, stated that as a chemical engineer, he is not aware of the type of radiation that a cell tower gives off causing health concerns. He stated that the radiation emitted is less energy than visible light. He stated that he is in favor of the request and suggested that the additional tower is needed to provide needed wireless service for the surrounding area. He suggested that the it is proposed in an appropriate location. He asked that the request be approved.

Ms. Susan Matthews, member of Parkers Landing POA, expressed concern with health issues and child safety, but does not see that this would be a health issue or that the request would affect property values. She asked that the request be approved.

Mr. Daniel Gingrich, 1621 Oak Crest Drive, expressed concern that the boosters previously mentioned have a short range. He stated that he has trouble with service in his home. He suggested that if aesthetics is a concern, there are different designs such as towers that look like trees that can be considered. He asked that the request be approved.

Mr. Hill stated that the penetration rate of radio frequency is minimal and there has been no evidence that it causes health issues. He stated that they did look at different locations, but the proposed location was considered the best option to provide the best service for the area. He stated that the different designs were also considered, but the stealth tower is considered the best option and would provide service to a greater area. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne closed the public hearing.

Mr. Cuttino asked the required distance the tower must be from residential uses. Ms. Canon answered that the distance from residential must be equal to the height of the tower.

Mr. Millet asked what consideration the Board has. Ms. Canon answered that the request is a PD amendment so the Commission has the option to either approve the request, approve with conditions, or deny the request. She stated that if approved, it would be a permitted use allowed within the PD.

Mr. Wren moved for approval of the request. Ms. Campaigne seconded the motion.

Mr. Wren agreed that the wireless service is very poor in the area. He stated that as a father with small children, he is concerned with health and safety, but has not seen any correlation of cell towers causing health issues.

Ms. Smith agreed that there has not been evidence that the cell towers cause health issues. She stated that wireless service is now a vital part of life.

Mr. McNeill suggested that there are not sufficient reasons to deny the request.

Ms. Campaigne stated that she is concerned with health and safety issues as well, but suggested that there is not sufficient evidence that cell towers cause health issues.

Mr. Cuttino suggested that the need for cell service in the area outweighs any minor radiation concerns.

Ms. Campaigne called for a vote on the motion. All in favor with Mr. Chapman abstaining.

The Board convened at 6:24 pm for a short break and reconvened at 6:26 pm. Planning Commission

Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 2 & 3). Mr. Neal asked which properties are zoned R-2 in the surrounding area. Ms. Canon showed the zoning for the surrounding properties on the map for the Commission. Mr. Neal asked which properties are non-conforming. Ms. Canon answered that she did not have information on the exact number but based on the map it appeared there were multiple non-conforming lots.

Ms. Smith asked if redevelopment of the lot under R-2 zoning is precluded if the structure is removed. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that any new structure would have to comply with the R-2 zoning standards and uses, which does not allow duplexes.

Mr. Wren asked if the property could be subdivided if it remained under the R- 3 zoning. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that the units are attached. Mr. Wren asked if the adjacent public housing is still owned by the City of Charleston and if the zoning is R-2. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Mr. McNeill asked if the surrounding property is zoned R-2. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Campaigne asked if the adjacent property has apartments or duplexes. Ms. Canon answered she was unsure if they were multi-family or duplexes.

Mr. Nick Collins, representative for the applicant, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that the property was purchased with the duplex existing. He stated that because of fire and water damage, the entire structure needed to be demolished. He stated that they would like to rebuild the duplex and have similar affordable housing available.

Mr. Neal asked if it was previously a duplex. Mr. Collins answered in the affirmative and stated that it has been a duplex for the past 20 years. Mr. Neal asked if there are other duplexes in the area. Mr. Collins answered in the affirmative but was not sure of the exact location. Mr. Neal asked if the units would be affordable housing. Mr. Collins answered in the affirmative and stated that they do not intend to change the building from its original design. Planning Commission

There being no comments, Mr. Neal closed the public hearing.

Ms. Campaigne asked if the property is adjacent to apartments. Mr. Prause answered that he was not sure if the City of Charleston project pre-dates the R- 2 zoning designation. He reviewed the difference between townhouse, duplexes and apartments with the Commission. He stated that the zoning was designated in 1979.

Ms. Smith suggested that the apartments were existing before the zoning was established. She asked if it is required to bring a non-conforming lot into compliance if redeveloped. Mr. Neal answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Lehman asked if the duplex is “grandfathered in”. Mr. Prause answered that the use was allowed as non-conforming and would not have to be brought into compliance until after it met the 50% threshold. Mr. Lehman asked if this request was approved, would it set a precedence. Mr. Neal answered that there are apartments in the area and there are non-conforming lots as well. He suggested that there have been requests for subdivision of lots in the area with the desire to redevelop. He suggested that this changes the character of the neighborhood and he is not in favor of this. He stated that there have been occasions where rezoning was desired because it would mean a non-conforming use would then become conforming.

Ms. Smith suggested that subdivision was allowed when the lots met the lot requirements for the designated zoning.

Ms. Campaigne stated that she is in favor of having more affordable housing, but expressed concern with changing the zoning from what is seen with the surrounding neighborhood.

Ms. Gregg expressed concern with setting a precedent and that there would be subsequent similar requests.

Mr. Wren asked the difference between this property being in the overlay district and remaining zoned R-2. Ms. Canon answered that the overlay district allows reduction of the front setback. Planning Commission

Mr. Neal asked if this was denied, could there only be one unit on the lot. Mr. Prause answered in the affirmative and stated that there is a 40% lot coverage requirement.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that a single family unit could be constructed with an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) that could then be leased.

Ms. Smith moved for denial of the request. Mr. Millet seconded the motion.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that different structure types other than single family units should be considered to provide more affordable housing. She suggested that affordable housing is a critical issue and should be discussed during the update of the Comprehensive Plan.

Ms. Smith agreed but suggested that the current zoning should be taken into consideration. She suggested that approval of the request would set a precedent. She suggested that there is not a hardship for the request.

Mr. Neal suggested that there is a hardship in the fact that there was a fire and is in proximity to other apartments and multi-family units. He suggested that because there is no one at the meeting desiring to speak, there is no opposition to the request. He stated that he is in favor of more affordable housing.

Ms. Gregg suggested that this property not being in the historic district has a bearing on the involvement of the community. She suggested that the character is changing in this area because of not having the more stringent regulations.

Mr. Neal called for a vote on the motion. Motion passed on a 6 to 2 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Ms. Gregg, Mr. McNeill, Mr. Wren, Ms. Smith, and Mr. Lehman being in favor; Mr. Millet and Mr. Neal opposed.

(Ord. No. 17047) Mr. Gawrych moved for approval; seconded by Mr. Smith. Mr. Santos asked Ms. Farrell what can be built on Areawide Business and what can be built on what is being requested for the change in zoning. Ms. Farrell stated that Areawide Business is the requested zoning. She said this property is currently unincorporated so they are requesting to incorporate and zone Areawide Business. She said that it is a variety of different retail, office types of uses, because this is in the Urban Corridor and there is an allowance for some residential. She said it is a broad spectrum of uses, but not the more intense types of uses such as auto repair. Mr. Santos asked if a hotel could be built. Ms. Farrell responded in the affirmative. Mr. Santos asked if the properties adjacent to this property are also zoned as such, could a hotel go on their property as well. Ms. Farrell stated that this is the next item on the agenda, which is to request Areawide Business zoning for those properties as well. Mr. Santos stated that this is something that needs to be looked at, because many of the citizens are talking about hotels. He said

that Charleston has slowed down on building hotels and the Town appears to be building more. He added that the Comprehensive Plan Committee also needs to look at this when discussing the Comprehensive Plan. He said putting together these properties is going to provide an opportunity to build another big hotel and traffic and infrastructure needs to be reviewed in that area. He said that this is a very busy intersection and he and the citizens are concerned about this. Sean Barnes, 1418 Barbara Street, said that he is a local businessman and has been in business for 28 years. He said that he is the owner of Docks Unlimited and owns two lots on the right hand side. He added that he has a long-term lease on 1361 Old Georgetown Highway and owns the other lot. He said he builds docks and does aluminum fabrication. He said where Larry’s Locks used to be to the tip of that property is going to be a hotel. He said that it has already been purchased. He said that there is a gentleman that lives two blocks over that has a steel building and is not able to do anything with it, so he purchased it. He said since the new overlay, you are not able to build on your property until you are 75 feet off on one side and 50 feet back from Old Georgetown Highway. He said that he has been working on this property for a long time, but when the roadwork was redone, it took away the exit point and did a roundabout. He said now they have done something completely different and he is unable to turn around with a regular vehicle, so a firetruck cannot turn around. He said they allow them to cut through into the Old K- Mart, but this is not a real road. He asked how an outlet or access could be put in. Barry Wolff, 1468 Pocahontas Street said that this is part and parcel of what he said before in regards to the public not understanding the ramifications of the zoning. He said if the public was aware that these parcels were possibly being consolidated for the construction of another hotel, Council Chambers would be full.

Gary Berenyi, of Hoyt and Berenyi, said that this rezoning is consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and the intention is not to build a hotel, but an office/retail space/flex space and to have some flexibility which is consistent with everything in that area. Mr. Santos was opposed. All other present voted in favor. Mr. DeMoura read FIRST READING BY TITLE ONLY. 4.

She suggested that the project should not have been presented to the Commission. She stated that the maximum height for this property is 50 feet and not 80 feet as has been mistakenly reported.

Ms. Pat Sullivan, 1002 Plantation Court, stated that this is a southeastern coastal town where residents value history, character and environment. She suggested that the proposed project along the coastline is not appropriate at the presented height. She suggested that the project is ostentatious and not in character with the lowcountry. She suggested that the height should not be compared to the Yorktown control tower. She suggested that there should have been a Planning Committee

collaborative effort with the Town and the community on this project to ensure that the project would meet the Town’s requirements.

Mr. Gary Santos, 1690 Greystone Blvd, stated that after seeing the design of the project and the intended uses, it seems that there could be an opportunity to partner with Patriots Point and not duplicate efforts between the museum and the Yorktown that would mean the ability to lower the height. Mr. Ulma reviewed the request with the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. Morrison reviewed transportation comments with the Committee (attachment 1).

Mr. Morrison answered in the affirmative and stated that the displaced parking of approximately 112 spaces would be the responsibility of the project with additional parking being paid for by the Town for a total number of parking spaces of approximately 170 spaces.

Mr. Bustos asked if there are any changes to the developer’s presentation from what was presented to the Planning Commission. Mr. Stuart Whiteside answered in the negative.

Mr. O’Rourke stated that his understanding is that the applicant is willing to work with the Town on revising the project to better meet the requirements of the Town. He suggested that this should go back to the Planning Commission to review the revised proposal. He stated that he would like to see this project come to fruition and suggested that this project should go back to the Planning Commission to receive a recommendation on the revised project.

Mr. Brimmer asked how many variances are included in the request. Mr. Ulma answered that there are some considerations such as the proposed changes to the Impervious surface setback from 30 feet to 15 feet, with an average of 30 feet; maintenance of the critical line buffer at 15 feet; and the extended height to 140 feet. He stated that some other minor variances involve parking lot landscaping. Planning Committee

He stated that there has been a preliminary Design Review Board (DRB) staff review as well to provide some insight into the proposed design guidelines. Mr. Brimmer agreed with Mr. O’Rourke’s comments. He stated that as a former Planning Commission member and now Town Council member, he has been reviewing plans for over ten years. He suggested that the item should be deferred or withdrawn in order to work with the Town and have more community outreach so that there is a better consensus and approval on the project. He agreed that more work should be done to ensure a better project. He suggested that deciding now would not be beneficial for the Town or the project.

Mr. Bustos stated that there are a lot of “moving parts” with this project including the relocation of the road, which requires a signed agreement that is currently not in place. He agreed with the previous comments where all the variables are not currently known. He suggested that the project should be completely vetted before a decision is made to ensure that the citizens, Town Council, and the developer are comfortable moving forward.

Mr. Joe Daniels, Board CEO, thanked the Committee for this opportunity and the privilege to work on this project. He agreed that the only way this project comes to fruition is through an engaged partnership with the community and the Town. He stated that he understands the impact a project as this could have on the quality of life. He stated that there should be opportunity for the community to provide input on this project.

Mr. Brimmer asked about the procedure with either a deferral or withdrawal. Mr. Ulma suggested that if changes are anticipated, then the project should be withdrawn and resubmitted. He stated that Town Council would need to approve a waiver to submit within the one year waiting period.

Mr. Bustos suggested that the request could be deferred for 60 days with the project to come back to the Committee. He stated that then a decision could be made on whether it would need to go back to the Planning Commission for a public hearing.

Mr. Brimmer agreed and suggested that the applicant should determine if it should be deferred or withdrawn. Mr. O’Rourke agreed and stated that once deferred, the applicant could choose to withdraw. Mr. Daniels agreed. Planning Committee

Mr. Brimmer moved for deferral of the request for up to 60 days with the request to come back to Committee. Mr. O’Rourke seconded the motion. All in favor.

No. 18004) Mr. Ulma stated that this is a rezoning request for approximately seven acres of land on the south side of Rifle Range Road and the request is to change the zoning from CC, Community Conservation to R2, Low Density Residential District. He stated that Town Council reviewed this at the January Council meeting and referred it back to the Planning Committee for additional review. He said the future land use designation is Low Density Neighborhood and limits the overall density to no more than three dwelling units per acre. He said the requested district is listed in the plan as one which can be considered in this land use plan designation. He said the request would be to change the existing CC Community Conservation zoning to R-2. He said current zoning allows lots of 12,500 square feet or larger and the minimum lot width is 80 feet with a depth of 110 feet. He said the requested zoning has lot sizes of 8,000 square feet minimum, widths of 60 feet across the frontage and the depth must be at least 90 feet. He stated that the applicant previously explained that the district would allow greater flexibility using the smaller lot sizes and reduced setbacks. The Planning Commission provided no recommendation to Council on a tie vote and the Planning Committee had no recommendation, which is when this came to Council at the last meeting. He said one of the primary items of discussion was access to the lots in the existing subdivision to the east. He said a copy of a plat was provided and showed a fifteen-foot ingress/egress easement running along the common property line adjacent to this property. When it went back to the Planning Committee, there was additional discussion and the members also did not provide a recommendation due to a 2-2 vote. Mr. Matt Schrimm, 1440 Melvin Bennett, expressed concern with commercial property affecting his property as it is adjacent to the proposed property. Ms. Mamie Rudy, 1232 Melvin Bennett, expressed concern with the proposed commercial portion would back up to their residence. She expressed concern with child safety. She stated that there is a huge historic oak on the property and does not want the tree to be removed or impacted.

Ms. Campaigne asked if the buffer between commercial and residential would be more substantial than if it was residential adjacent to other residential. Ms. Canon answered that no buffer would be required between single family uses. Ms. Campaigne suggested that having commercial use with a buffer would better preserve the wooded character and “feel” of the lot and surrounding area as it currently exists than if there were only residential uses.

Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2). Planning Commission

Mr. Wren asked what the Commission vote was for the previous request for this property in January. Ms. Lynes stated that she would check the minutes. Mr. Wren asked if there is a survey or sketch plan delineating where the division of the property would occur. Ms. Canon answered that a rendering was included with the application but a sketch plan has not been submitted at this time.

Mr. McNeill asked the difference between AB and AB-2 zonings. Ms. Canon reviewed the differences between the zonings for the Commission.

Mr. Neal noted that the main difference between the zoning designations is the ability to have outdoor storage as a special exception.

Ms. Lynes answered that the Planning Commission recommended approval at the January meeting on a 7 to 2 vote.

Mr. Tim Askins reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. McNeill asked what the property would be utilized for. Mr. Askins answered that it would be used for a commercial office. Mr. McNeill answered that due to the size of the lot and the number of trees on the lot it would be difficult if zoned Office Professional (OP).

Mr. Neal asked if the request can be conditioned. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the negative. Mr. Neal asked if the property can be deed restricted. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren asked if the deed restriction would be a civil matter. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the affirmative.

Mr. McNeill asked if the deed restriction could be removed. Mr. Pagliarini answered in the affirmative based on how the restriction is worded.

Mr. Shaun Rudy, 1228 Melvin Bennett, suggested that the property should remain residential. He expressed concern that there is no definite plan for the property. He suggested that more residential would be preferred to a commercial use. Planning Commission

Mr. John Burn, 1411 Breckon Road, stated that he owns the property adjacent to the requested property. He stated that Bowman Road is a well-traveled roadway and suggested that a residential use would not be preferred next to and adjacent to other commercial property. He suggested that the surrounding residents would not want additional traffic on Melvin Bennett. He suggested that this is a good opportunity and the request would be consistent with the surrounding uses.

Mr. Larry Heigg, Moss Park, expressed concern with the property being zoned commercial and that it would set a precedent and increase traffic along Melvin Bennett Road. He expressed concern with not knowing what uses would be on the property. He suggested that any proposed uses should be consistent with the surrounding neighborhood. He stated that he is opposed to the request.

Mr. Askins stated that he has correspondence from the surrounding residents and distributed these to the Commission (attachment 3). He suggested that the deed restrictions would be done as a good faith effort and after consulting legal advice, would be done in perpetuity.

Mr. Neal asked if a buffer would be located between Mr. Rudy’s property. Mr. Askins answered in the affirmative and stated that he has been speaking with the owners about increasing the buffer in that area. Mr. Neal stated that the neighbors have expressed concern and suggested that an agreement should be secured if possible.

Mr. Lehman asked if Mr. Askins lives in the neighborhood. Mr. Askins answered in the negative.

Mr. Millet asked if any of the correspondence from the residents in favor of the request live on Melvin Bennett. Mr. Askins answered that some of the residents live across the street with their property fronting on Bluebird, but backs up to Melvin Bennett. Planning Commission

Ms. Gregg asked the reason for not requesting Neighborhood Commercial (NC). Mr. Askins answered that NC has a 6,000 square foot building maximum. Ms. Gregg asked if one reason for the request is to maximize parking. Mr. Askins answered that they prefer to construct one building at 7,500 square feet so that the parking is more accessible. Mr. Askins answered that the difference would be the amount of parking required and the restriction of uses. He stated that AB zoning would allow more flexibility in uses allowed on the property.

Ms. Smith moved for denial of the request. Mr. Millet seconded the motion.

Ms. Smith suggested that this is considered spot zoning. She suggested that this issue should be considered through the Comprehensive Plan process.

Ms. Canon clarified that the request was not previously denied, but the request was withdrawn by the applicant.

Mr. Wren asked for clarification on spot zoning. Mr. Pagliarini answered that this would not be considered spot-zoning.

Mr. McNeill asked the zoning of the county property. Ms. Canon suggested that it was residential but did not have a definitive answer.

Mr. Neal expressed concern with the access extending across the property line and how this could be remedied. Mr. Mitchell answered that the easement would be on the property line. Mr. Pagliarini stated that an easement does not currently exist, only a driveway.

Mr. McNeill asked where the curb cut is located. Mr. Mitchell showed the location on the plat for the Commission. Mr. McNeill asked if the two properties would share the existing curb cut. Mr. Pagliarini answered that an additional easement might be necessary as well.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that the easement would be on the requested property. Ms. Smith agreed and stated that the driveway would need to be moved. Mr. Mitchell agreed.

Ms. Gregg asked if the easement would be recorded. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative and suggested that other elements as noted in the staff comments should be included on the plat as well. Ms. Gregg asked if there is a way to have both future parcels conforming. Mr. Mitchell answered in the negative.

Mr. Millet asked what is adjacent to the requested parcel. Mr. Mitchell answered there is a car wash on the south parcel and the north parcel is vacant. Mr. Millet asked if there is access to the car wash. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Neal moved for approval of the request including all staff comments with the added condition that a satisfactory easement and access plan in accordance with Town roadway standards to be approved by the Transportation Department. Mr. Cuttino seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal asked if Fire Department approval would be needed prior to the Transportation Department giving final approval for the roadway. Mr. Mitchell answered that the information and all approvals are provided prior to approval of the final plat. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne asked about buffers. Mr. Neal suggested that the buffer is included in the staff comments. Mr. Mitchell stated that staff noted that if a buffer was desired, it should be included in the approval.

Ms. Smith moved to amend the motion to establish a 50-foot buffer along US17 for the newly created lot. Mr. Wren seconded the amendment.

Mr. McNeill suggested that there is currently a 30 foot easement and asked if the buffer would be outside of the easement.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that the buffer should include the easement.

Mr. McNeill suggested that if the property were commercial, a 20-foot buffer outside of the easement might not be sufficient.

Mr. Neal suggested that a larger buffer would be too onerous.

Ms. Gregg asked if the requested buffer width is standard.

Mr. Wren asked what the buffer requirements are. Mr. Mitchell answered that it would be 100 foot width for major arterials with a minimum 50 feet width for collector streets and minor arterials.

Mr. Millet asked for clarification on the requested buffer and if the 50 foot buffer requirement would include the easement. Mr. Wren answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the amendment. Motion passed on a 7 to 2 vote with Ms. Campaigne, Ms. Gregg, Mr. Wren, Ms. Smith, Mr. Lehman, Mr. Millet and Mr. Cuttino in favor; Mr. McNeill and Mr. Neal opposed.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the amended motion. All in favor. Planning Commission

Mr. Mitchell and Mr. Bernard reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. McNeill asked about lots 4-9 and if access would be from Jackson Street. Mr. Mitchell answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren asked about access for lot 10. Mr. Mitchell answered that it would be from the easement (hatched section).

Mr. Cuttino asked about the trees near lot 7 and lot 9. Mr. Bernard answered that they are a laurel oak and live oak.

Mr. McNeill asked who owns the right-of-way. Mr. Bernard answered that they are state streets.

Ms. Campaigne suggested that SCDOT approval could be stipulated in the motion.

Mr. John Tarkin reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that they would like to preserve as many trees as possible including some pine trees that have sentimental value.

Mr. Millet asked if the applicant would be amenable to having a sidewalk on Jackson Street. Mr. Tarkin answered that he is not opposed to a sidewalk, but if constructed, the sidewalk would not connect to an existing sidewalk and would mean significant trees would need to be removed.

Ms. Smith stated that staff did not recommend a sidewalk on Jackson Street and suggested that impervious surface should not be increased in this area.

Mr. Wren asked if the trees in the right-of-way can be preserved. Mr. Tarkin noted that tree removal is not necessary for installation of driveways. the trees would be preserved if possible but wanted to have the option in the event they needed to be removed.

Mr. Neal asked about the laurel oak by the easement for lot 10 as well as the other trees between lot 9 and the easement and asked if they can be better preserved. Mr. Tarkin answered that the easement is 20 feet wide, but the driveway would only be twelve feet wide and would have pervious material of sand shell or plantation mix. He stated that the rendering shows a more meandering driveway so that the trees are not as impacted. Mr. Neal suggested that the lot 9 property line should be moved so that the trees fall within the HOA property and preserved. Mr. Tarkin answered that this could be done.

Ms. Campaigne commended the applicant on the smart design and the preservation of the trees for the property. Mr. Tarkin stated that they would mitigate all of the protected trees removed but would like to preserve as many trees as possible. He stated that there is a bio-swale and garden to the rear of the property that would carry runoff to the dry pond.

Mr. Wren asked about the trees not included on the submittal. Mr. Wooddy answered that the original tree survey had some incorrectly labeled trees. He stated that the revised tree survey is correct.

Mr. Wooddy reviewed the reasoning for the LDR waiver request with the Commission. ➢ Topography and pattern of the lots—there is a natural low area near lot 10 and significant trees. He stated that rather than regrade the area that would alter the drainage pattern and impact the protected trees, the access easement was determined the best option. ➢ Detrimental to adjacent property—He stated that the only property not developed is to the north and a pipe drainage easement is being provided for future development. ➢ Protecting health, safety, and welfare—He stated that the storm drainage system along Jackson Street flows into the low area of this property. He stated that improvements proposed would increase the storm coverage to 50% which is above the required percentage.

Mr. Neal asked the width of lots 5-8 compared to lot 9. Mr. Tarkin answered that lot 9 is approximately 20 feet wider than the other lots. Planning Commission

Ms. Gregg asked if lot 5 and 6 are buildable given the canopy of the protected tree. Mr. Tarkin answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Wren asked how the Old Village drainage study improvements would impact this property. Mr. Mitchell answered that the property is within the Royall Avenue basin and there would be improvements in the near future in the area including along Jackson Street.

Mr. Cuttino asked about landscaping and how it would be maintained. Mr. Tarkin answered that it would be maintained by the HOA.

Mr. McNeill asked how the maintenance would be accomplished. Mr. Neal suggested that the property could be deed restricted through the HOA.

Ms. Campaigne moved for approval including staff comments; emphasizing the desire for the applicant to work with staff so trees currently shown on lot 9 are protected by adjusting the lot line between lot 9 and the proposed easement with final approval by staff. Mr. Neal seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal asked if the motion is intended to have the trees located in the HOA property. Ms. Campaigne answered in the negative and stated that she would not want the better quality trees to be potentially impacted because of moving the lot line.

Mr. Wren amended the motion to include preservation of trees 54 and 39 with SCDOT approval. Mr. Neal seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal asked how the motion can be amended when the trees are in an SCDOT right-of-way. Mr. Pagliarini answered that this cannot be done and therefore the amendment is not valid.

Mr. Wren withdrew his amendment. Mr. Neal withdrew his second.

Mr. Neal asked if motion includes sidewalks on Jackson Street. Ms. Campaigne answered in the negative.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor. Planning Commission

Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachments 1 & 2).

Mr. Jody Peele stated that the Town is in the process of securing a consultant to complete a Public Services master plan.

Ms. Smith suggested that it would be beneficial for the Town to reach out to the community to provide more information on what is proposed in the future, transportation issues, etc. Mr. Peele answered that a better idea of how the property would be utilized would be known once the master plan was completed. He stated that there are no plans to use this property as a transfer yard.

Mr. Neal asked if it is beneficial to defer annexation and zoning until the master plan is completed. Mr. Peele answered that they would like to complete the master plan based on the ordinances in place for the property and that it would be better to have it annexed and zoned within the Town.

Ms. Gregg asked what current activities are being conducted on Six Mile site. Mr. Peele answered that there are five divisions working out of the Six Mile Facility: stormwater, waste management, facilities, grounds, and infrastructure. Ms. Gregg asked what a transfer yard entails. Mr. Peele answered that all garbage goes to a landfill or commercial drop-off site. He stated that any vegetative material is transported to the Six Mile Facility, reloaded and then transported to the Bees Ferry landfill. He stated that by doing this, it keeps as many vehicles in Mount Pleasant working throughout the Town.

Mr. Darien Mackey, 3605 Purple Martin, asked if the requested property would be used as a transfer station. Mr. Wren answered that it was indicated that it would not be used as a transfer yard.

Ms. Tamarae Tabaka, 3774 Copahee Sound Dr, expressed concern with the property being used for a dump site and that it would be detrimental to the Planning Commission

quality of life for the surrounding neighborhood. She stated that Lieben Road is a narrow two-lane road with no signal onto Hwy 17. She asked that the property be buffered and screened. She asked that the main entrance of the property be located off Hwy 17 and not on Lieben Road and that a signal be added to the intersection of Lieben Road and Hwy 17 as well.

Ms. Charlotte Pollard, 1558 Periwinkle Dr, expressed concern with there being increased truck traffic, particularly with the proximity of Wando High School. She suggested that Lieben Road is the “jumping off point” of a cultural corridor and suggested that this would not be an ideal location for this type of use.

Mr. David Tabaka, 3774 Copahee Sound Dr, suggested that it is premature to approve this request since it is not known how the property would be used.

Mr. John Frahalla, 1530 Macoma Dr, expressed concern with their only being one access from Hwy 17 to the entire neighborhood. He suggested that the zoning should not be determined until the master plan is completed. He stated that it is a pedestrian-friendly neighborhood. He stated that there is only one access into the neighborhood and expressed concern with having a commercial use at the front of the neighborhood.

Mr. Edward Tabor, 3767 Tipp Lane, agreed with previous comments and expressed concern with increased truck traffic in the neighborhood, particularly with the potential for increased truck traffic in proximity of the schools.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing.

Mr. Neal asked if the transportation concerns can be addressed through the completion of the master plan including buffers, screening, increased truck traffic, etc. He also asked if the property is annexed but the zoning denied, what would the default zoning. Mr. Peele answered that the property has already been purchased. Mr. Rutherford answered that the property would be zoned R-1 which does not allow outdoor storage. Mr. Neal asked if there are plans to use the property within the next 60-90 days. Mr. Peele answered that the Public Services Department does not have any plans for the property at this time, but the property is currently being utilized by the Fire and Police Departments. Planning Commission

Ms. Campaigne expressed confidence in the Town being able to address all concerns. She stated that there is a difference in the county requirements from the Town requirements and suggested that there is a risk that the master plan would have to be redesigned if completed under the county requirements.

Mr. McNeill asked if there are any other options than PI-2. Ms. Canon answered in the negative and stated that this is the most compatible zoning for future use of the property. Mr. McNeill asked if it would be used as a transfer yard. Mr. Peele answered that the proposed property is not large enough to support a transfer yard and the Six Mile facility is more centrally located and serves the Town well.

Mr. Millet asked if any other location has been considered. Mr. Peele answered that this property was purchased with the thought that it would be the best location to serve the community. Mr. Millet suggested that the requested zoning does not fit the community. Mr. Peele stated that the master plan would determine what uses are located at that location. Mr. Millet suggested that the master plan should be determined before moving forward. Mr. Peele noted that the Six Mile facility is located within a residential area and works well within a mainly residential area. He stated that it will take some time to determine the master plan and what would be located on the property. He stated that at this time, he does not have any concrete plans. He stated that the property was purchased to provide a location to better serve the Town in that area.

Mr. Wren asked how many dwellings could be located on the property if it were zoned R-1 residential. Mr. Rutherford answered that it could allow approximately 15 homes. Ms. Canon noted that the future land use recommends Public Institutional (PI), so a Comprehensive Plan amendment would be needed to establish density if zoned differently. Mr. Wren asked if the requested zoning was denied, would the zoning then be non-conforming based on the Future Land Use Map and Comprehensive Plan. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Smith suggested that this move forward, with the Town working with the community as the master plan is completed.

Mr. Neal stated that this would be a recommendation to Town Council and asked what the next step would be on the design so that the public can provide Planning Commission

input. Mr. Rutherford answered that property zoned PI does not require Design Review Board approval; it would be reviewed and approved by staff.

Mr. Neal moved for approval including all staff comments. Mr. McNeill seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal asked about if the two adjacent roads are town roads and fully constructed and does Lacannon connect to Hungryneck Blvd. Mr. Rutherford answered that the roads are county roads and Lacannon does not connect to Hungryneck Blvd. He stated that both roadways are not fully constructed.

Ms. Smith asked how the violation was determined. Mr. Rutherford answered that it was determined through a windshield survey of the property. Ms. Smith asked if there have been any neighborhood complaints. Mr. Rutherford answered in the negative. Ms. Smith asked how long the violation has occurred. Mr. Rutherford answered that the AB zoning was consistent with the existing use of the property at that time. Mr. Millet asked what the underlying zoning is. Mr. Rutherford answered that it is AB.

Mr. McNeill asked what is located adjacent to the property. Mr. Rutherford answered that it is an orthodontist office. Mr. McNeill noted that there are commercial uses surrounding this property. Ms. Smith asked about outdoor storage on some properties on the same road. Mr. Rutherford answered that the property is in the county.

Mr. Gates asked if the submittal should be accurate and are considered legal documents. Mr. Pagliarini answered that staff reviews the submittal to determine if the application is complete.

Mr. Greg St. Pierre, applicant, reviewed the request with the Commission. He stated that they are not opposed to remaining in the HNB-VR-OD. He stated that there have been no complaints from the neighbors on the current use of Planning Commission

the property. He stated that they are requesting the rezoning to bring the property into compliance.

Mr. Neal asked if the reason for the request is because of a code violation. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the affirmative. Mr. Neal asked if there is a privacy fence around the property. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the affirmative and stated that there is an eight-foot privacy fence with landscaping. Mr. Neal asked how the property is accessed. Mr. St. Pierre answered that there is access from Venning Road and Lacannon Lane. Mr. Neal asked if the access is paved. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the negative and stated that it is a gravel road.

Mr. Millet asked about the boat storage. Mr. St. Pierre answered that they allow boat storage in the overflow parking areas. Mr. Millet asked if they charge for the boat storage fee. Mr. St. Pierre answered in the negative.

Mr. Neal stated that he is supportive of the request as it would bring the property into compliance.

Mr. Millet asked about the removal from the HNB-VR-OD. Ms. Canon answered that staff explained the requirements of the HNB-VR-OD with the applicant prior to their submittal. Uses, to a 6.58 acre parcel identified by TMS No. 558-00-00-933. (Ord. No. 18048) Ms. Whitley moved for approval; seconded by Mr. Brimmer. Mayor Haynie asked if this changes the amount of development or is it only the uses. Mr. Ulma stated that it adds some additional uses based on requests for potential tenants they have been working with. Mr. Cunnane asked if the parking requirements were reviewed prior to the changes made to the PD. Mr. Ulma responded in the affirmative and added that the uses are similar to the other uses that were allowed. He stated that staff did not focus on the need for additional parking. He stated that it is also an issue as they get tenant fit-ups in particular buildings and it is something that staff reviews to ensure that the proposed use and the situation with parking gets addressed. Mr. Cunnane stated that when it was approved there was significant discussion on how many spaces each apartment should have as well as each store, which is why he is having some angst over it. Mr. Ulma stated that the net differential would be minimal. Mr. Santos asked Transportation Director, Brad Morrison if they have completed any type of research on the trip counts. He said that workout studios are very popular and asked how much affect this will have on trip counts that were originally done for this area. Mr. Morrison stated that he has not reviewed this particular issue; however, the trip generation assumption was either specialty retail or shopping center, so all the uses being discussed are included within that trip generation rate. He stated that as long as you are not considering converting retail into general office, then there would be no difference. He stated that these are all uses that are within a shopping center use, so the trip rate

makes those assumptions that there are broad uses and averages this. Mayor Haynie asked if this was a backdoor way for someone to pay one level of impact fees, then change the use and generate more trips than what they have paid impact fees for. Mr. Owens stated that they would have a change in use if that were the case. Mr. Morrison responded in the negative. He stated that when the use comes in for a building permit, this is when the applicant pays for the use at that time. Mr. Owens stated that he believes the calculation for parking spaces for these facilities is 300 square feet per parking spot. Mr. Ulma stated that it ranges from one space per 200 square feet of use or one space per 300 square feet. He stated that on the paperwork for this item, the spaces required when originally approved was 1,108 and they are providing an additional 40 spaces than what was required. Mr. Owens asked if there is any shared parking in this complex for commercial. Mr. Ulma stated that it would all be shared within. He said in terms of impact fees, all of the buildings in the retail area are already under construction and would have paid their impact fees based on a shopping center designation. Mr. Santos was opposed. All others present voted in favor. Motion to approve carries 8-1. Mr. DeMoura read FINAL READING BY TITLE ONLY. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED this date. 3.

tms-580-14-00-003~planning~R-23-18~0:
Ms. Canon reviewed staff comments with the Commission (attachment 1).

Mr. Neal asked the status of the Longpoint Road realignment project. Ms. Canon answered that the section between Rifle Range Road and Billy Swails Parkway would move forward, but the section from Boone Hall would no longer occur as directed by Town Council. Mr. Neal asked if any of the realignment would occur. Ms. Canon answered that at this time it would not move forward as originally proposed but alternatives are being studied.

Mr. McNeill asked if the project would not move forward because the project would have required a portion of the Boone Hall property to accomplish the realignment. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative.

Mr. Gates asked if the overlay district would remain. Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative. She stated that the overlay districts are being reviewed as part of the Comprehensive Plan update process.

Mr. Kevin Berry, Earthsource Engineering, and Tommy Baker, developer, reviewed the request with the Commission. Mr. Baker stated that they have been working with the community to ensure their concerns are addressed. Planning Commission

Mr. Neal asked about the park portion and if it would be deeded to the Town. Mr. Baker answered that the property would be owned by the bank and be available for community and public use.

Ms. Smith asked who would be responsible for maintenance of the park. Mr. Baker answered that as the property owner, he would be responsible for the maintenance of the park.

Mr. Gates asked if there would be drive-thru. Mr. Berry answered in the affirmative. Mr. Gates asked if the community reinvestment act requirements would be completed. Mr. Baker answered that they have met all the federal requirements for the community bank.

Mr. Lehman asked if there would be dedicated parking for the park. Mr. Baker answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Mary Forman Jackson stated that her family previously owned the requested property. She stated that she is a sweetgrass basket maker and is an avid promoter of the sweetgrass basket industry. She stated that she is in favor of the request and having a bank located on the property. She asked for all those in audience in favor of the request to stand.

Mr. Lewis Jefferson, vice-chair of CAGE, stated that they have met with the developer and are in support of the project. He suggested that the guidelines of the Comprehensive Plan should be adhered to and is confident that this project would adhere to all the requirements.

Reverend Gallant stated that he has been working with the developer and CAGE to ensure that the project comes to fruition and addresses all the community concerns.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed the public hearing.

Mr. Neal asked if the Sweetgrass basket stand location would be included with the project. Mr. Baker answered in the affirmative. Planning Commission

Mr. Wren asked the reason a bank use is not allowed in Limited Office (LO) zoning. Ms. Canon answered that LO is more appropriate for transitional areas and allows more low impact office uses where there is not a lot of customer traffic, such as an insurance or other type of professional office. She stated that based on the traffic, a bank would be a higher impact use.

Mr. Neal asked if it could not remain in the Sweetgrass Basket Overlay District (SB-OD). Ms. Canon answered in the affirmative and stated that the overlay district requirements would take precedence that would prevent a bank use. She stated that this would limit square footage, limit to LO uses, and restrict hours of operation. Mr. Neal asked if there are residential uses to the north of the property. Mr. Berry answered that there are commercial uses next to the requested property; there is no residential in close proximity. Mr. Neal asked about the triangular parcel. Mr. Berry answered that it is separately owned and currently vacant.

Mr. McNeill asked what other uses would be allowed in Office Professional (OP) zoning. Ms. Canon reviewed the uses allowed under OP. She stated that a restaurant, gas station, or vehicle sales would not be allowed.

Ms. Smith asked if the current design would allow for the Longpoint Road alignment in the event the project was approved in the future. Mr. Berry answered that the alignment should not impact the current proposed location.

Mr. Neal moved for approval of the zoning and Comprehensive Plan amendment including all staff comments. Mr. Cuttino seconded the motion.

Mr. Neal stated that the staff comment regarding the artifacts should be addressed.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

providing for an amendment to the Watermark Planned Development District Ordinance (Ord. 05052) by amending the Zoning Map to incorporate an approximately 1-acre parcel located on Bowman Road to allow for AB, Areawide Business uses with the addition of outdoor storage in association with Car Rental Office use. (Ord. 25026) April 23, 2025 Planning Commission Minutes May 5, 2025 Planning Committee Minutes Ms. Reed presented the request to incorporate a 1-acre tract of land into the Watermark Planned Development. The property, currently zoned AB (Areawide Business), fronts Bowman Road just off Chuck Dawley Boulevard. The applicant wanted to allow for car rental with outdoor display/storage of rental vehicles. Rather than rezoning to AB-2, which would allow more intense uses, the applicant proposed to join the Planned Development with limited conditions allowing just the car rental use. The Planning Commission had recommended approval with an enhanced buffer—a full 25-foot buffer with an 8-foot masonry wall— along the residential portion of the property line. The Planning Committee made no recommendation. A motion to deny was made by Councilwoman Hyatt and seconded by Councilman Chapman. During discussion, Councilman Rambo noted that the property would be developed regardless, and the current proposal with enhanced buffers would be less intensive than many other allowed uses under the current zoning. Councilwoman Hyatt expressed concerns about deed restrictions that had been promised when the property was originally rezoned from R-1 to AB-1, which appeared to prohibit vehicle rental with outdoor storage.

Mr. Pagliarini clarified that the town could not enforce private deed restrictions, though residents could seek enforcement through civil courts. Mayor Haynie called for a vote and the motion to deny failed with a 4-4 vote. Councilwoman Hyatt and Councilmen Chapman, Iacofano and Santos voted in favor of denial, with Councilmen Brownstein, Rambo, Tinkey and Mayor Haynie voting opposed. (2)

No. 20001) Ms. Canon stated that the first request is to annex and zone a property at 2161 Annie Laura Lane. She stated that this property is currently in the County and in the Mount Pleasant Overlay district and also the underlying zoning in the County is S3, which is a Special Management 3 district which is similar to the Town’s Community Conservation zoning.

Mr. Santos moved to approve; seconded by Mr. Chapman. Mayor Haynie stated that he will be opposing this which is not based on the application but because certain values of homes cost the taxpayers and the treasury more than what they deliver in tax revenues. He said the piecemeal annexation of properties may be to the benefit of a new annexation, but to the detriment of the rest of the taxpayers. He said there needs to be a more comprehensive approach. tms-558-00-00-249~planning~R-28-19~4:
to zone R-3, Medium Density Residential District, an approximately 0.34 acre tract of land located at 2161 Annie Laura Lane. Property is not proposed to be included in the SB-OD, Sweetgrass Basket Overlay District. (Ord. No. 20002) Ms. Canon stated that the second portion of this is to request an R3 zoning district. She said the comprehensive plan calls for community conservation, so if it were automatically annexed into the Town, it would be assigned Community Conservation and the Overlay would not automatically be applied, so they would be required to be included in the Overlay District. She said this request is to bring the subject parcel in, zone it R3 which is in character with the other parcels shown in brown in the zoning map. Mr. Rambo moved to approve; seconded by Mr. Chapman. Mr. Chapman stated that there are before and after pictures of this neighborhood and a number of improvements were done. He said he sat on the Planning Commission when a presentation was made about cleaning up the neighborhood and improving a number of lots on the far end of Gulf Drive which did not connect at that time with Annie Laura Lane. He said they recognized that this was not an ideal place as it existed but it could be made an ideal place although it is relatively close to the Town’s Public Services site. He said there are issues living next to a Public Works site that have all of the refuse trucks being cleaned and brought in on a daily basis. He said the property owners took a chance to improve a part of a neighborhood, because this was in a conservation district and similar to some of the areas which the Town calls settlement communities. He said people want to bring in their families to live on larger lots and Mr. Sanchez wishes to do so on this site. He said there are new sidewalks, new waterlines and how substantially improved the area currently is. He said this request is simply another piece of this and 94 properties in the area have already been annexed

into the Town and the process should continue to make this part of Mount Pleasant and no longer be a donut hole. Mr. Rambo stated that the illustrations show how many properties along Annie Laura Lane currently have the R3 residential zoning. He said you cannot single out one parcel. He understands the need for community conservation and at some point, they should have a stopping point. He said this whole street is already this way. Ms. Landing stated that we would like to bring as much property into the Town as possible, because good things come from this. She does not believe that this one resident should be penalized for what could happen down the road. Mayor Haynie stated that the Town is facing the stark reality of what it costs to provide services to single family residential and will look closely at this during the Budget Committee meeting tomorrow. He said if homes of this value cost the Town more in services than they bring in, when this property is subdivided, then it is doubled. He realizes these are hard decisions. Ms. Whitley, Ms. Corley, Ms. Hyatt and Mayor Haynie were opposed. Ms. Landing, Mr. O’Rourke, Mr. Rambo, Mr. Santos and Mr. Chapman were in favor. Motion to approve carries 5-4. 3.

Mr. Rob Turquoise, attorney with Rice Motley, stated that cell towers have non-ionized radiation and early studies did not provide sufficient information on the effects of cell tower radiation on health. Mr. Kevin Berry and Mr. Dan Sherer reviewed the request with the Board.

Mr. Kichanan asked about the proposed future office building and that it would be too close in proximity to the proposed building. Mr. Berry answered that it is only showing potential future building area with a shared courtyard. Mr. Berry asked about the sidewalk and how it would connect to the parking. Mr. Berry showed this on sheet C-200 for the Board.

Mr. Seabrook asked about parking for the future building and if the site could provide sufficient parking. Mr. Berry answered in the affirmative and stated that they would have the parking be more linear as recommended by staff. Mr. Seabrook stated that he is not opposed to a 50-foot buffer on the front.

Mr. Wurst asked if the attic space would be used and if the pitch of the roof could be lowered. Mr. Sherer answered in the negative and stated that this could be considered. Mr. Wurst also suggested that the gables could be lowered as well.

Mr. Seabrook asked for clarification on comment #12 and if the existing service needs to be relocated. Mr. Luly answered that the route should be relocated so it does not go through the buffer. Mr. Berry stated that they are not opposed to re-routing the sewer line. Mr. Seabrook suggested that there could be restrictions and suggested that trees should be preserved as much as possible. Design Review Board

Mr. Wurst suggested that roof line should be lowered. He suggested that the columns appear thin and the windows under the gable should be combined. He suggested that the water table should be restudied and lowered to ensure a window is not sitting in that table.

No. 22017) January 19, 2022 Planning Commission Meeting Minutes January 31, 2022 Planning Committee Meeting Minutes Ms. Whitley moved for final reading, seconded by Mr. Iacofano. Mr. Chapman said there is a plan for access into the property from the rear, and that was part of the plan as it was developed for the entire Carolina Park project. He stated the developer planning this in their present location continues to have vehicles parked in the buffer zone as late as this weekend, and extensively. He would like to ask if it is possible to have a clause for this amendment if they do the same thing on this site where they are parking vehicles in the buffer zone. He asked if it is possible to do this to force them to keep the vehicles out of the buffer zone. Ms. Reed said the reason this was not on the consent agenda is because Mr. Chapman stated he would like to make some amendments such as no parking in the buffer and no future plans for a left turn where the median is located. She stated because it is a planned development amendment, we could attach those conditions, and asked Mr. Pagliarini to confirm. Mr. Pagliarini stated that is correct. Mr. Chapman moved to add those two amendments to make sure we do not get left turns in or out, and to require no parking in the buffer zone, and if they do park there, that entrance closes. Mayor Haynie asked if no parking in the buffer zone is already covered by an ordinance, and perhaps it is just an enforcement issue. Ms. Reed said if they violate this condition or this zoning provision, she does not know if that would change anything in the approved planned development. She said it would be a code enforcement issue. Mr. Pagliarini stated the Town would have the right to enforce within the context of the planned development so he feels it is relevant if Mr. Chapman would like to include it. Mr. Chapman moved to amend the ordinance so that in the future, no left turns would be made in or out of this development at location F, and second, in the event we have the same problem in the current location, that the direct access to 17 be closed. Mayor asked for clarification if Mr. Chapman was referring to the right turn in, and Mr. Chapman concurred. Mr. Chapman said enforcement had a very difficult time trying to get the vehicles out of the buffer area, and he is putting this in here because they worked for over two years to try and get the vehicles out of there. He said other dealerships were staying outside the buffer so there is no reason for this. Ms. Whitley seconded the motion. Mr. Pagliarini stated for clarification that we cannot close access for a violation. Mayor Haynie said that would affect the second part of Mr. Chapmans amendment and asked Mr. Chapman if he would like to strike that part. Mr. Chapman amended his motion to strike the closing of the access for violations. Ms. Whitley amended her second. After further discussion, Mayor Haynie called for the vote on the amendment and Mayor Haynie, Mr. Chapman, Ms. Hyatt, Mr. Ritchie and Ms. Whitley voted in favor with Ms. Corley, Mr. Santos, Mr. Rambo and Mr. Iacofano voting opposed. The motion for the amendment carried with a 5-4 vote. Mayor Haynie called for the vote on final reading of the amended ordinance and all present voted in favor. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED this date

tms-532-03-00-022~planning~R-13-22~0:
TMS no. 532-03-00-022 is currently zoned R-1 Low Density Residential, requesting to rezone to R-3 Medium Density Residential. Parcels identified by TMS nos. 532-03-00-031, 532-03-00-030, 532-03-00-107 all currently zoned R-2 Low Density Residential District requesting rezoning to R-3 Medium Density Residential as well.

Mr. Stone reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Ms. Kelsey Santiago and Mr. Buzzy Branbill, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Ms. Kate Womble, 1037 North Shem Drive, stated that she and many of her neighbors are opposed to the request. She expressed concern that the rezoning would mean smaller lots, more density, and more traffic. She suggested that if approved, this request would mean an approximate 50% increase in density. She expressed concern with pedestrian and child safety, drainage, and flooding. She asked that the current zoning remain to preserve the neighborhood.

Ms. Angela Burchfield, 942 South Shem, expressed opposition to the rezoning and asked that the request be denied. She stated that many in her neighborhood are opposed to the rezoning as it would increase density. She stated that there is a petition signed by the residents in opposition of the request and asked that the residents’ request be upheld.

Mr. Frank Toler, 949 South Shem, expressed opposition to the rezoning request. He suggested that the current zoning should remain. He suggested that the rezoning request is in opposition of the Comprehensive Plan. He also expressed concern with drainage and that this project would exacerbate the issue.

Ms. Kara Campbell, 955 South Shem, expressed concern with drainage and asked that the request be denied.

Mr. Mike McCullough, 1125 Sea Island Crossing Way, stated that he is opposed to the request. He expressed concern with pedestrian and child safety. He suggested that the project would increase traffic and endanger the children. He suggested that improvements are needed before additional Planning Commission

development is approved in addition to the sidewalks being connected for the area. He asked the Commission to deny the request.

Ms. Patricia Blair, 1166 BB Lane, expressed concern with the request. She stated that she is opposed to the request. She expressed concern that the request would increase traffic and cause additional vehicular accidents. She expressed concern with child safety. She suggested that BB Lane is a private road, and that this development would be detrimental to her property and her quality of life.

Ms. Kim Berkheimer, 1182 Russell Drive, stated that BB Lane is a private roadway. She suggested that if the request is approved, there is not sufficient infrastructure to support the development and it would increase traffic for the area.

Mr. David Bedair, 1156 Russell Drive, Lot 23, asked that the request be denied. He suggested that there is already significant traffic in the area and would increase with the development. He expressed concern with drainage and suggested that development would increase the drainage issues in the area. He asked that the project be denied.

Mr. Joe Bustos, 649 King Street, agreed that the residents have been well spoken. He stated that he supports the requests from the neighborhood for denial of the request. He expressed concern with increasing traffic in the area.

Mr. Reese Artigues, 1047 Governor Road, stated that the property is currently zoned to allow up to 40 homes. He stated that the proposal is to reduce the number of homes to 20 homes. He suggested that the main cause of traffic is the nearby school and is only during the morning and afternoon school days. He suggested that he has met with the applicant and the applicant expressed a desire to meet with the school to review the project. He stated that he supports the request.

There being no further comments, Mr. Wren closed public hearing.

Ms. Santiago noted that the number of homes would be significantly reduced. She stated that they are willing to work with the staff to meet the drainage and tree requirements and have already started discussion. She Planning Commission

stated that they are also working with MPW regarding water and sewer. She stated that they understand the historic tree issue and stated that they want to preserve the trees on the property as much as possible.

Ms. Smith moved for denial of the request. Mr. Davis seconded the motion.

Ms. Smith suggested that this is an infill project. She suggested that there is an obligation to the existing neighborhoods to protect them from increased density. She also noted that there are drainage issues in the area that should be addressed as well before more development is approved. She suggested that the current zoning should remain.

Mr. Davis suggested that the project would cause “overdevelopment” of the property and agrees with Ms. Smith’s comments.

Mr. Wren agreed that the requested zoning is not compatible with the neighborhood.

Mr. Wren called for a vote on the motion. All in favor.

providing for an amendment to the Wilson Tract Planned Development District Ordinance (Ord. No. 95041) pertaining to property known as Towne Centre Shopping Center Further proposed is to rezone and incorporate an approximately 0.75-Acre parcel from AB, Areawide Business District, into the Towne Centre District of the Wilson Tract PD, Planned Development District. (Ord. No. 25044; Exhibit A) Councilmember Rambo moved for denial, seconded by Councilmember Hyatt. Councilmember Chapman engaged Planning Director Michelle Reed in detailed discussion about current entitlements. Reed explained the property's AB (Area-wide Business) designation allows 4 units per acre plus an additional 4 if dedicated to attainable housing. She clarified that while theoretical entitlements exist, practical limitations include triggering impact assessments (at 75 peak hour trips and 40,000 sq ft commercial), building height restrictions (35 feet), parking requirements,

and open space requirements. Reed estimated approximately 130 residential units could be built by-right without triggering an impact assessment, along with 40,000 square feet of commercial. Chapman expressed concern about traffic from commuters, stating if anybody has been at the bottom of the Ravenel Bridge and see all of the cars coming into town every morning, most of them come here to work. He advocated for workforce housing, arguing employees honored for longevity could actually live in the town of Mount Pleasant. However, he criticized being whiplashed into deciding between Belk's and the owners and noted the planning committee and commission had wrestled with what we felt was appropriate for the future. He expressed frustration that despite council being accused of shutting Belk's down and shutting down the movie theater, which couldn't be further from the truth, they must still address the situation. Chapman suggested deferring to have the two sides work together quickly to settle this issue. Councilmember Iacofano expressed frustration about being placed in the middle of what seems to be some kind of lease dispute. He acknowledged something needs to be done with Towne Centre but felt the conceptual designs were too vague. He noted Planning Commission had recommended approval with conditions including: height limited to 55 feet on exterior, 60,000 square feet dedicated to family entertainment if Regal closes, 14% green space (up from 10% shown), 6 market rate to 2 attainable housing units ratio, and 2 designated incubator locations. Iacofano recognized the developer had made many requested changes over 4 years but concluded there's still work to be done. Councilmember Hyatt stated the item came before council without committee recommendation due to unforeseen circumstances and the applicant's request. She objected to just a request for entitlements without a plan, emphasizing once we do that, it doesn't come back to us. It is out of our hands. So we're signing away any control over what we end up with. Councilmember Brownstein acknowledged cracks in the foundation of Towne Centre citing the vacant Bed Bath and Beyond and lack of evening foot traffic. Mr. Rambo moved for first reading, seconded by Mr. Santos.

Mr. Chapman asked Ms. Reed to explain the commitment by the applicant to not do anything else with respect to the AB use at this location. Ms. Reed stated there are two buildings which were used as a construction office. The front building was office use, and the equipment was stored in the back. She said if there is any redevelopment there, or they make a 50% improvement to the property they would need to install the fifty-foot Mathis Ferry Road side-buffer. providing for the annexation of an approximately 0.93-acre parcel located at 1490 Boston Grill Road, depicted on a plat recorded by the Charleston County ROD Office in Plat Book BE, Page 27. (Ord. No. 26002) Planning Committee recommended denial.

Town Council Meeting Town Council Meeting Ms. Reed presented the next two items explaining that these ordinances would annex and zone a 0.93-acre parcel on Boston Grill Road. She noted that the property is located within the Hamlin Beach historic designation and would be zoned as CC (Community Conservation). The Planning Committee had recommended denial of the annexation, but

Town Council Meeting should it be annexed, both the Planning Commission and Committee recommended the CC zoning. During discussion, Council Member Tinkey expressed concerns about annexing properties from historic communities, noting that areas like Brickyard, Seaside, and the Old Village have protective overlays that prevent such actions. He emphasized that these historic settlements dating from after the Civil War deserve similar protections and mentioned that the town has been working for three years on establishing equivalent historic overlays. Council Member Rambo disagreed with this perspective, arguing that denying annexation would not prevent development. He explained that if annexation is denied, Mount Pleasant Water Works would still have to provide water and sewer by law, allowing development to proceed without town impact fees or taxes. He questioned the argument that these communities should have protection similar to HOA neighborhoods, pointing out that not all neighborhoods have HOAs and not all property owners want to be included in historic overlays. Ms. Reed clarified that three settlement communities east of the Cooper (Hamlin Beach, 10 Mile, and Phillips) already have historic designations in the county. She explained that 10 Mile Community recently completed work to draft and adopt a zoning overlay, and that Hamlin Beach would be the next community to develop such protections, followed by Phillips. She noted that town staff are working to determine how the town could adopt the same historic overlay and whether that might involve creating a joint commission. After further discussion about the timing of potential historic overlay protections, the Mayor indicated he would vote with the Planning Committee's recommendation to deny the annexation. A roll call vote was conducted on the motion to approve the annexation. Motion to approve the ordinance was made by Council Member Rambo and seconded by Council Member Chapman. Council Members Brownstein, Whitaker, Chapman, Hyatt, Rambo and Iacofano voted in favor with Council Members Crosby, Tinkey and Mayor Haynie voting opposed. The motion carried with a 6-3 vote. (3)
