tms-560-02-00-047~planning~R-05-26~3: to rezone from OP-2 Office Professional-2 District to R-3, Residential District, two parcels located on the corner of White Flat and Bowman Road, consisting of approximately 0.47 acres in aggregate as indicated in Charleston County Plat Book BU, Page 130, and Book EB, Page 333. (Ord. No. 26016) Planning Commission recommended approval; Planning Committee recommended denial. Ms. Reed presented the request pertaining to two properties at the corner of Bowman and White Flat Road, currently zoned OP2 office professional. She provided history that before 2019 they were zoned R1 historically. The structure was constructed without proper permits as a commercial building, and to make it right, town staff and council worked with the previous owner and rezoned to office professional. There were further issues with the building regarding parking, buffers, and meeting commercial codes, so it sat vacant since that time and changed ownership. The current request was to zone it back residential, but instead of R1, the request was for R3. These were two separate parcels under same ownership. R3 would allow duplex dwelling and single-family detached, while R1 only allowed single-family detached. In light of a text amendment later on the agenda dealing with density, these parcels would only be eligible based on square footage for single-family detached for each one, but R3 was more appropriate given property sizes - one was 11,000 square feet (suitable for R1), the other 9,000 (more like R2), but they could have single-family or duplex under R3, though based on size they were likely only to get one unit on each lot. Council Member Chapman noted this parcel had been an issue for quite some time, going back to when he was on the Planning Commission years ago, and they were no better off today than then. He thought that was reason to deny and put this in conjunction with others in the neighborhood to help protect it. Ms. Reed mentioned that when speaking with residents living behind there, they would like it to remain R1. Since it fronted Bowman Road, they were opposed to R3 density at the front of their neighborhood. Council Member Brownstein asked about the applicant's earlier comment that you could not fit an R1 lot on those properties. Ms. Reed explained these were legally established lots that were historically zoned R1. If the owner came in to subdivide, that would be an issue, but these lots had been in place and could likely get building permits. The larger one at 11,000 square feet met R1 requirements of 10,000 square feet. The smaller at 9,000 would not quite meet the threshold but could get certain variances from setbacks as a nonconforming lot. Council Member Rambo asked about the comprehensive plan and future land use. These were designated mixed neighborhood, which allowed R1, R2, R3, R4, townhouse, or multifamily, so any would be appropriate. Council Member Hyatt confirmed they were currently office professional and asked if they could do mixed use like office with apartment upstairs. Ms. Reed said the problem with the current building was trying to have commercial use and meet parking and buffers. Originally, they were approved because they purchased a lot across the street for parking, but they went to the board of zoning appeals in 2023 to get variances from parking, buffers, and setbacks, and were denied. Ms. Reed said perhaps if they demolished the building and put a much smaller building depending on use, they could meet requirements. Council Member Hyatt moved for denial, seconded by Council Member Chapman. All present voted in favor. (4.)

tms-558-00-00-161~planning~R-08-26~2: providing for an amendment to the Johnson Tract Development PD-MU-SU (Ordinance No. 14084, as amended), also known as Indigo Square by permitting Drive-Thru uses on an approximately 1.10-acre parcel located at the corner of Highway 17 North and Indigo Market Drive. (Ord. No. 26020) Planning Commission recommended approval; Planning Committee recommended approval. Council Member Whitaker moved for approval, seconded by Council Member Crosby. Ms. Reed explained this was an amendment to the Indigo Square planned development district ordinance. Several years ago in 2023, this was all one property owned by Olive Branch AME Church zoned R1. They zoned the church property PI1 and broke off a parcel just over an acre, incorporating it into the PD. It was established with a 15-foot buffer adjacent to Wando East townhomes, maximum size restrictions for office or neighborhood commercial uses. It was back for one change - for restaurant use, they wanted the ability to have a drive-through. Both the commission and committee felt comfortable recommending approval because the transportation impact assessment ordinance changed so any use with drive-through now required a transportation impact assessment, providing extra scrutiny through the transportation department. Mayor Haynie recalled a further caveat from Planning Committee about natural buffer of existing trees. Ms. Reed confirmed the 15-foot buffer requirement from the 2023 amendment, with the addition that if there was existing vegetation, keep it and add to it rather than clear to create buffer. Council Member Chapman recalled being on the Planning Commission when Indigo was approved and they specifically denied any drive- through. However, things had changed, and there would be an impact statement done to minimize impact in the segment between where they wanted the restaurant and the actual intersection. He asked about vacant land with trees between the restaurant location and the intersection remaining in place. Ms. Reed stated that was all church property, and while they intended future improvements, there would be required buffers anyway. Council Member Chapman noted it was significant distance from the US 17 intersection, continuing restrictions from when Indigo was originally approved, unlike the original desire to put something right at the intersection. Mayor Haynie called for the vote and all present voted in favor. (6)

tms-580-00-00-319~planning~R-16-26~0:
Mr. Stone reviewed staff comments with the Commission.

Mr. Bennett asked how the AMI is calculated and if it is adjusted over time. Mr. Stone answered that typically there is a range between 80%-120% AMI. Mr. Bennett asked if it periodically adjusted. Mr. Stone answered in the affirmative and stated that currently the planned development stipulates a cap of 80% AMI. Planning Commission Agenda

Mr. Benjamin Brown, Gregory Ferry Towns HOA president, reviewed the request with the Commission.

Mr. Bennett asked if the HOA voted for approval. Mr. Brown answered in the affirmative. Mr. Bennett asked the rationale for the one opposition. Mr. Brown answered that he is not sure the reason for the one owner being opposed. Ms. Erin Stampe stated that she did speak with the one in opposition, and there were some language barrier issues that once resolved, he was comfortable with the request.

Mr. Berry asked if all of the owners are under the 80% AMI. Mr. Brown answered in the negative and stated that there are some units that had different requirements. He stated that this request would mean that all of the units would have the same AMI requirements. Mr. Berry asked if there are different ranges for dual income households. Mr. Brown answered in the negative.

Mr. Barber asked if raising the AMI defeats the intent of the attainable housing. Ms. Ireland suggested that having a bigger range allows for more families to qualify for the housing. Mr. Brown stated that the goal is to have the attainable housing and having the larger range allows for a larger price point so those families moving on to their second home can have a larger profit margin to help them be able to purchase a larger home for their needs.

Ms. Ireland asked if only a certain profit margin is allowed or a maximum sale price. Mr. Brown answered that there are restrictions on the sale price of the housing and that only a certain percentage increase is allowed.

Mr. Barber asked what the original price point was for the homes. Mr. Brown answered that the cost of the dwellings varies.

Ms. Ireland suggested that there is a formula for calculating the sale price. Mr. Brown agreed. Ms. Ireland suggested that increasing to the 150% AMI is a reasonable request.

Mr. Barber asked what the sale price would be if sold at market rate. Mr. Brown answered that he is not sure.

Mr. Berry asked if there is a non-profit agency that calculates the sale price. Mr. Brown answered that it is based on the HUD requirements. Planning Commission Agenda

Mr. Bennett suggested that the request was reasonable.

Mr. Berry stated that there is a precedent and other neighborhoods that have the increased range.

Ms. Myra Richardson, 2755 Earl Johnson Lane, stated that the average sale price was $240,000-$310,000 for attainable homes. She suggested that the attainable housing should be priced to allow for housing for teachers and the public service industry and the AMI set to allow that workforce to be able to afford the homes.

Ms. Margaret Tierney, 1260 Allusion Lane, stated that as a teacher, she would not be able to afford the homes based on her salary alone.

Ms. Pleshette Grant, 1684 LaTroy Ave, suggested that having the attainable housing and the settlement communities preserved should be encouraged. She suggested that having the historic overlay district can help in retaining homes for generations.

Ms. Kendle Grumbles, 1038 Allusion Lane, stated that she was fortunate to be able to buy her home on a single salary. She suggested that it is difficult to buy a home in Mount Pleasant based on the current market.

Ms. Hattie Bailey, Mallard Lakes, stated that the school district should consider including housing that is restricted to public service workforce or giving a housing allowance to help retain the workforce.

There being no more comments, Mr. Bennett closed public comment.

Mr. Barber expressed concern with allowing such a significant increase.

Mr. Berry suggested that it is not allowing a higher price for the home, but having an increased number of qualified buyers. He suggested that increasing the AMI would potentially provide for a larger “pool” of buyers.

The Commission discussed the pros and cons of increasing the AMI. Planning Commission Agenda

Ms. Ireland moved for approval. Mr. Davis seconded the motion. Motion passed on a 6 to 1 vote with Mr. Smyth, Mr. Bennett, Mr. Davis, Mr. Berry, Ms. Mansour, and Ms. Ireland in favor; Mr. Barber opposed.
tms-580-00-00-319~planning~R-16-26~1:
Median Income Limits, for Gregorie Ferry Towns Attainable Housing development.

Mr. Stone reviewed the request with the Committee. He stated that the Planning Commission recommended approval.

Mr. Tinkey stated that he reviewed this with the Planning Commission chair and thanked staff for their review of the request including the scenarios.

Mr. Tinkey moved to recommend to Town Council approval. Ms. Crosby seconded the motion.

Ms. Whitaker asked the maximum sell threshold. Mr. Stone answered that it is 3% not including the approved qualified improvements. He stated that Origin SC, a non-profit organization, handles the calculations for the resale. Ms. Whitaker stated that she understands that the homeowner’s goal would be to sell the home for the maximum amount to have funds to put toward their next home purchase; however, the Town’s goal is to have housing available for first-time buyers. She expressed concern with increasing the AMI for this neighborhood as it would affect the amount of affordable housing available in the Town. She stated that she is aware of the different mortgage qualification criteria and that it can be difficult to secure a mortgage while still meeting the 80% AMI, but the intent is to have affordable housing at this price point within the Town.

Ms. Crosby agreed with Ms. Whitaker and asked if increasing the AMI would exclude a potential buyer. Mr. Stone answered in the negative and stated that once a home is purchased it does not have to be vacated if the household income increases above the 80% AMI. He stated that increasing the AMI would expand the number of potential buyers for the homes. Ms. Crosby expressed concern that increasing the AMI could mean that the homes would eventually reach fair market value, which is against the intent of having the affordable housing.

Ms. Whitaker agreed and suggested that it shifts the demographic from low income to middle income. Planning Committee

Mr. Tinkey asked if the potential buyer is required to report all household income. Mr. Stone answered in the affirmative.

Ms. Hyatt asked the ranges for the different tiers. Mr. Stone stated that these ranges for affordable and workforce housing are recognized by HUD; the attainable housing is a newer category. He reviewed the difference between affordable, workforce, and attainable housing AMIs with the Committee. She expressed concern with increasing the AMI to the attainable housing range. She suggested that while it would increase the number of qualified buyers, it would mean fewer opportunities for those at the lower income level.

Mr. Tinkey withdrew his motion. Ms. Crosby withdrew her second.

Ms. Crosby moved to recommend to Town Council approval of changing the AMI for Gregory Ferry Towns up to 120%. Mr. Tinkey seconded the motion.

Mr. Tinkey asked how this would affect the neighborhood and have any detrimental effects. Ms. Reed answered that up to 120% AMI is a typical standard. She suggested that the AMI for Carolina Park is outside the norm. She suggested that this being a more conservative and restrictive amendment, it would not require an additional public hearing. Mr. Pagliarini concurred.

Ms. Hyatt called for a vote on the motion. Motion failed on a 2 to 2 vote with Ms. Crosby and Mr. Tinkey in favor; Ms. Hyatt and Ms. Whitaker opposed.

Ms. Hyatt stated that this would move forward to Town Council with no recommendation.

tms-580-00-00-319~planning~R-16-26~3:
providing for an amendment to the Gregorie Ferry Landing PD-MU-SU (Ordinance 06082, as amended), specifically pertaining to the Attainable Housing Development’s definition of Affordable Units. (Ord. No. 26036) (Ord. No. 26036 FINAL) Town Council Meeting

Director Reed noted that this item had received first reading the prior month and was subsequently returned to the Planning Committee for further discussion. The amendment pertained to the definition of Affordable Units within the Attainable Housing Development. Council Member Daniel Brownstein moved to amend the ordinance to cap the total area median income at 120 percent, which was seconded by Council Member Iacofano. Council Member Kathryn Whitaker stated her opposition, citing that the development opened in 2020 with an intended AMI of 80 percent or below, that a unit sold in the current calendar year for $367,500, and that nontraditional financing programs such as South Carolina Housing and Fannie Mae Home Ready exist to assist sub-80 percent AMI buyers. She expressed concern that raising the income ceiling shifts the target population from low-income to middle-income households and does not address the town's broader need to diversify housing price points. Council Member John Iacofano expressed support, noting that the workforce housing AMI band of 80 to 120 percent is specifically intended to serve teachers, firefighters, police officers, health care workers, and hospitality employees. He further argued that the underlying formula is broken because it does not account for rising interest rates, which effectively disqualify 80 percent AMI buyers from obtaining conventional mortgages. Council Member Brownstein agreed with Council Member Iacofano's interest rate argument and added that even a Charleston County teacher Town Council Meeting

earns above the 80 percent AMI threshold, and that a married couple would find it exceptionally difficult to qualify. He stated that the amendment maintains, rather than shifts, the original intent of the development. Council Member Alex Crosby supported the 120 percent figure, noting that the original concept was intended to provide a pathway to homeownership and equity, not a permanent residence, and that current homeowners must be able to sell in order to give the next family the same opportunity. Mayor Haynie called for the vote and Council Member Whitaker voted opposed with all others present voting in favor. The motion carried 8-1. This Ordinance SIGNED, SEALED and DELIVERED, this date. (2)

Ms. Harris asked what the impact would be for schools in the area. Mr. Yowell answered that given the number of town homes proposed, the impact to the local schools would not be significant.

if staff has reviewed this proposal in terms of traffic. Mr. Stone answered in the affirmative and stated that no additional improvements were needed. Mr. Yowell suggested that more detail calculations were included in the traffic analysis.

Mr. Davis asked when the development construction would commence. Mr. Yowell answered that it depends on the review process but estimates in nine to twelve months.

Mr. Gilmore asked about sustainability improvements for the site. Mr. Yowell answered that there is tree preservation, wetland preservation, and 14% green space that is above the required percentage is proposed. Mr. Gilmore asked if other aspects such as permeable paving, solar roofs, etc. would be included. Mr. Yowell answered that these will be considered as the development moves forward. Mr. Gilmore asked about walkability. Mr. Stone answered that pedestrian connections would be included with Mount Pleasant Way and/or Highway 41 improvements, which is a joint SCDOT and Town project. Mr. Gilmore asked about pedestrian access to the commercial uses and suggested there should be careful consideration for inclusion and connection.

Mr. Ed Trevisani, 1192 Sharpstowne Court, and President of Porcher Preserve HOA, stated that they are in support of the proposal. He suggested that the proposed 87 town homes would be more compatible than the previously approved commercial plans. He stated that there is a proposed reduction in traffic of approximately 60%, which is an important consideration for Porcher Preserve. He suggested that the information presented would be more compatible and mean fewer peak hour trips and traffic. He stated that the proposed improvements to Porcher Bluff Road and the Highway 41 improvements will provide relief in the area needed. He asked for the proposal be approved.

Mr. Andrew Harris, 1160 Sharpestowne Court, stated that he supports the request as well. He stated that the developer is a quality builder with a quality product that has high aesthetics. He suggested that having the residential component would help to support the exiting commercial uses. He state that Planning Commission

Billy Swails Parkway is in the area and provides pedestrian access to Laing School and provides areas for the students to walk and ride their bikes to Laing School. He suggested that once Mount Pleasant Way is completed it will connect to the commercial areas as well.

There being no further comments, Mr. Bennett closed the public hearing.

Mr. Barber asked about the impacts to the Town in terms of services provided by the Town. Mr. Stone answered that he is not sure of the contrast between commercial and residential for services such as water and sewer and trash. Mr. Stone answered that multi-family is considered a commercial use in terms of tax revenues.

Ms. Ireland stated that she appreciates the concerns for traffic. She stated that the Comprehensive Plan recommends changing commercial zoning to residential and that this is essentially being done with this request. She stated that hotel uses were designated certain hubs, including the Market at Oakland. Again, this request would remove that use. She further stated that the townhomes would not be attainable housing and would increase the number of cars and traffic in the area. She expressed concern about the density and that the number of homes would increase the density in the area. She suggested that having a mixed use with commercial uses would allow 4 units per acre on the second floor or higher, with an additional 4 units per acre if attainable housing, but this is not being requested. She suggested that the request should not be approved.

Mr. Barber suggested that there are other options for development for this site other than what has been proposed.

Mr. Bennett suggested that the residential would make the PD more mixed use. Mr. Barber suggested that mixed use would be different uses within the same building. Ms. Ireland stated that Town Council recently denied a townhome development near commercial off Highway 17 that was like this proposed development. She suggested that the proposed is not mixed use. Mr. Bennett suggested that from a practical standpoint, the proposed development is adjacent to retailers and has walkability to those uses. Planning Commission

Mr. Bennett moved for approval as presented with the findings that although not attainable housing, it would serve a niche within the housing market that is not well filled at this time. Also, the proposed development would have fewer trips and less traffic. Mr. Smyth seconded the motion.

Mr. Barber suggested there is more opportunity for this area that could be more beneficial. He suggested that it should remain open to more commercial development or a more true mixed development.

Ms. Harris suggested that the implication and impact to the schools should be considered. She suggested that the density seems high when considering the school impacts.

affirmative. Mr. Tinkey suggested that some affordable housing should be included. He expressed concern with the buffers and suggested that they should be larger. answered that it is approximately 1100 feet. Ms. Ireland stated that the land development regulations limit the length of the roadway to 1,000 linear feet. Mr. Mitchell concurred and stated that the turnaround breaks up the roadway, so the linear foot maximum is calculated from the point of the turnaround. Ms. Ireland suggested that an LDR waiver would be needed to deviate from the maximum length allowed. Mr. Mitchell answered that this was a staff determination made because of having the turnaround. Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Losse Knight, architect representing the applicant, stated that they are proposing to remove the existing shed structure and replace with garage structure. He stated that the lot is an irregular shape and are trying to propose a new footprint for the carport relative to some of the setback requirement for grand trees and turning radiuses for getting in and out of the property. They wanted to demonstrate that although they are asking for this structure to be within 3 feet of the setback, it is fairly consistent when you view the accessory structures that are already in the general area. He showed the existing structure they are proposing to take down. They would like to propose a simple open air, structure with columns in the front with a small storage area in the back, which will also function as an entryway into the home. He stated that the area along the side property line is where they are asking for a 3 foot setback and the typical accessory setback is 6 feet. The building is turned so as you move away from the corner they are 5 feet off the setback on both sides and along the rear, they are 4.7 feet. Mr. Keenan asked what the building’s current setbacks are. Mr. Knight said that it is 6 feet on both sides. They are attempting to have a dual carport and entry. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Dickson asked if they took the storage element away, would they have their 6 feet. Mr. Knight stated that likely on that area, but one of the purposes of this is to pick up some storage. He stated that there are allowances in the guidelines to have a 12 x 12 structure in other areas on the site; however, when you look at turning radius and setbacks for tree protection, there was no other place to put the structure. The roofline is set at 18 feet and trying to keep with the architectural character of the existing roof. Ms. Dickson asked if there was room under the eaves for storage. Mr. Knight stated that there is, but very little. The original intent was to think about a full height space, but realized that they were exceeding 18 foot threshold. Their goal is to review height, scale and mass, but also would like to receive feedback on the footprint of the structure. Ms. Dickson asked if Mr. Knight has talked to the neighbors about backing right up to their property line. Mr. Knight stated that they have not. Mr. Keenan stated that they are basically asking for a 3 foot encroachment variance from this commission. Ms. Dickson asked if they needed it on both sides. Mr. Knight stated that on the rear side, they are encroaching roughly 18 inches, so it is 4’7” off the rear setback. One side will be 3 feet and the rear side would be 18 inches. Mr. Keenan stated that everything on those lots are very tight and this lot is very complicated. Mr. Bennett stated that what Mr. Knight has drawn is consistent with what was discussed over the last several weeks in terms of design and the more modest height of accessory structures. He applauds what Mr. Knight has done; however, has reservations that given the way the lot is situation and the fact that the applicant already has some encroachment to the rear anyway, is a 3 foot variance meaningful. Ms. Rowe asked how large the storage area is. Mr. Knight said 6’10 in one direction and 14 feet in the other. Mr. Knight stated that the initial study was a 2 car garage and realize that this would not work. They tried to study other buildings around and decided to go to an open carport and have a little bit of storage in the back. They could potentially consider pulling it forward to move it away from the rear accessory setback. However, it would detract from the hierarchy of the main house and make the carport front and center. Ms. Rowe asked if they thought about doing something similar to the house on Bennett Street with the storage on the side and the open front and back. This would accomplish storage. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Knight stated that they did like that one; however, it was setup for a width of approximately 22 to 24 feet in order to make this work. This lot is a really irregular site. Mr. Keenan stated this his thoughts are consistent with Mr. Bennett’s and appreciates the 18 foot height and likes the open air aspect and understands this is a function of storage and being able to cover their vehicle. Is 3 feet that big of an issue? He does not believe so. Ms. Dickson stated that she would like to know what the neighbors think, because it may be an issue for them. Claudia Coker, homeowner, stated that the storage is important because they have bicycles, paddles for kayaks, skateboards, basketballs, and are not storing tools. She stated it is a very unique lot and this is all the way back in the corner where her neighbor to the right, his building is actually blocking his house from this structure. The neighbor behind, it is in the very corner of his lot where his kids play back there, but they have a full yard and also have an accessory building up against her property that is within the setback. She said she is asking for some leeway, because the neighbors’ buildings are within the setback and because of the uniqueness of her lot, there is no other way to do this. She does not think the neighbors would have an issue. Ms. Dickson stated that granting a variance is easier when they know that the neighbors are okay with it, because you are asking for relief from the rules as they stand. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the reservation he has is the nature of the lot and the continuum of houses in that area are shoehorned in. To add an additional structure that is in excess of the setbacks it pushes the envelope further, especially without property feedback from the neighbors. He stated that it feels that too much is being put into a space that has already surpassed its utility. Mr. Knight stated that he understands that they have not addressed the neighbors, but thought that this was a platform for it to be publically addressed where it is put on the internet, with the yellow sign out in front of the home. He stated that in the future, do they need to be knocking on the doors of neighbors. Mr. Keenan stated that this is that platform and the Commission will not make decisions based on what the neighbors are thinking, but based on the guidelines. However, supportive letters always help. Mr. Bennett stated that the Commission cannot require letters of support from an applicant; however, they are helpful. Mr. Knight asked if their preference which they thought would be the best option is to sit the structure back and ensure they are not overwhelming the house. Given that this is an open air type of colonnade and it does have a porch like feel, if they were to move it so they are at least not in the rear setback, they could completely get out of that. At that point, the front corner is out of it and they just have approximately 30% of the back corner. Old Village Historic District Commission

They have a hip roof that was intentionally designed to pitch away from the neighbor’s property instead of something that projects out. Would something like this be acceptable to be able to maintain a similar footprint? Mr. Bennett stated that this is a sample he would be more comfortable with, because then you are asking for inches instead of feet. The debate the Commission is having is adding another setback variance in this restrained tight space, which is already happening with some of the neighbors, or because the other variances have already been granted either explicitly or by default with the way things were built years ago, does the Commission just accept this for this particular tract and grant another 3 feet for another accessory structure. This is the dilemma that the Commission faces. For the applicant to make that concession towards the rear, he could be more comfortable with the setback variance on the other dimension. Ms. Rowe agreed. Mr. Bennett stated that the other issue is the setback ordinances are there for a reason and some of that is to provide separation and not impose on neighbors. The other is more practical as a matter of maintenance. Are you able to get back between those spaces to property paint and repair them and provide reasonable drainage. He stated that the Commission has been faced with this on a number of occasions.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Miles Beach, stated that Mary-Julia Royall was President of the Confederate Memorial Association for 20 years or more. This association dwindled to 2 individuals, Mary-Julia Royall and one other. He stated that she asked the Moultrie Camp Son of Confederate Veterans if they would take title to Carr Street Cemetery. He stated that Carr Street Cemetery includes a lot more than just that piece that is enclosed with wrought iron, which now needs some repair. He stated that 5 or 6 years ago, they were happy to take title to the cemetery and their attorney drew up the property documents and they have been registered and filed with the courts. Moultrie Camp 27 of the Sons of Confederate Veterans does own this property. Mr. Bennett stated that his understanding is it goes all the way through back to Royall. Mr. Beach stated that the block that Carr Street Cemetery is in probably has a fairly large number of graves there that they know nothing about. They had a state archeologist come from the State to do a scan of the entire property, which would indicate where unmarked graves are located. From the back of the fenced in portion, coming towards Carr Street, on the right hand side, from the oak tree forward, there are 11 unmarked graves. Their intent is not to do anything with this area. He does live in the OVHD; Old Village Historic District Commission

however, Mary-Julia Royall, to maintain the cemetery over the years, they felt that she needed some recognition for all that she has done for that cemetery. Before they put the sign up, the new house next to the property, has a driveway the ends before you get to the back of the house, and they have a stack of everything there, which is very visible. They removed all the barbed wire, vines, trash trees, etc., and opened it up and have come back in and planted camellias, azaleas, encore azaleas and several other to help hide some of the items that are at the new house. He showed an area that had become a trash area and they wanted to do away with the trash area. Another issue they had was with a resident who had a heating and cooling system that is down on the ground and uses the temperature of the ground to heat and cool the system. His overflow drain pipe goes out onto the cemetery property, which causes some issues. He stated that the sign in question is approximately 6 feet x 3 feet and is done is Charleston green and is set in concrete and they would like to recognize Mary-Julia Royall and this would be a very honorable way of doing so. Their request, although after the fact, is to allow them to leave the sign in place. Mr. Bennett stated that he applauds what the SVC BB – applaud what SCV is doing and to assume responsibility for this parcel. He stated that Mary-Julia Royall is a Town treasurer and to acknowledge her for her years of commitment is wonderful. His reservation about the sign itself is that it emphasizes a park and not clear what the park is and does not represent that it is a confederate cemetery. Mr. Beach stated that there is a sign on the fence that states Confederate Cemetery and has also put 2 signs from the Boy Scouts who are working on their Eagle Project. What they should recognize is the War of 1812 monument which is there. He stated that there are only 2 War of 1812 monuments in the in the State of South Carolina, and they have one, which is inside the fence. He believes the cemetery sign sets it aside. The entire property has underground irrigation from street to street and their intent is to make it a landscaped park with different trees and flowers. Mr. Keenan thought the sign placement was odd. Mr. Beach stated that they put it there to keep people from dumping their trash there. Out of respect for those graves, they wanted to stop the dumping of trash and it has worked. Ms. Rowe asked if the sign was level. Mr. Beach stated that it was and that the property has a slight slope to it that makes it look like it is not level. Ms. Rowe stated that it is a lovely monument to a lovely person. Ms. Dickson asked Mr. Beach if he has had discussions with the Preservation Society about putting up a property sign that tells the public what is there, such as the 1812 monument and the confederate cemetery. Mr. Beach stated that the 1812 monument is there already on the street side. He stated that they raise all the funds to maintain this cemetery, so Old Village Historic District Commission

funding is sometimes an issue. He stated that they do want one of the signs indicating that it is a Confederate Cemetery. Mr. Keenan made a motion to approve the ex post facto application for the Confederate Cemetery as submitted; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. John Linton, homeowner, stated that he and his wife are the homeowners. This house was his wife’s great aunt and uncle’s originally and is on a slab. He stated that they had two to four inches of water during Hurricane Matthew and had to rip out all the walls. He stated that it is in the VE flood zone so they are not able to repair it, because the value of it is diminimous. He stated that they are in a situation where they have to demolish and rebuilt, which is one of the basis for the demolition request. He provided photographs of their house in 2015 during the 1,000 year rain, and stated that the home is no longer appropriate for the area, which is an old concrete block house with no historical significance and Old Village Historic District Commission

not compatible with the surrounding homes. He provided plans for a two story home that is board and batten siding, and the size is modest compared to other homes in the area. He stated that they positioned the proposed home more towards the front of the street, similar to the other homes in the area and believe this will provide the view in accordance with the new guidelines for positioning of houses. He stated that this will actually be very similar. He stated that the driveway would be a pervious material. Mr. Hirshorn stated that for the demolition he would be inclined to grant it based on the criteria 1, 2 and 3. He stated that he is still contemplating the design of the new structure. Ms. Dickson stated that she is agreeable to grant demolition as well. Ms. Rowe is also agreeable with demolition. Mr. Keenan stated that he does not have an issue with the demolition based on the three criteria. He stated that he is not following the architectural design, but does like the size of the home. He does not have issue with the board and batten. Ms. Wilson stated that there is a disconnect with the massing pieces. There is a really strong tall gable form and because the other pieces are low, it is reading almost as a tower. She stated that it could be worked to be a little more harmonious. She stated that there is a small entry porch and in the Old Village entry porches are a real front presence and really important. She stated that we really have to fight for those porches and they sometime get undervalued, but especially on Pitt Street, it will be appreciated. She would like for the homeowner to look at the front porch size and its relationship to the building. She stated that it is coming in on the side and sees the access to where the vehicles are going to be, but this house needs to relate to the street a little more. The side gable, the pitches, and the massing is again a disconnect with the strong, very vertical gable facing Pitt Street. The second floor pergola seems unusual for the area. She stated that catching the distant water view and understands that, but struggling with it formally as opposed to having more of a roof or something with a pitch. Visually, from the street, it amounts to a flat roof porch, which is awkward and maybe it is shifted back a little more off the street if it is really important to the homeowner. In general, there is a lot of different massing pieces that are not working together and the house needs more of a front from Pitt Street. Ms. Rowe stated that it comes across looking more like a beach house. She stated that the second floor long rectangular window and the pergola does not seem harmonious. Ms. Dickson stated that she loves porches and is all for it, especially if you have a water view; however, this porch looks stuck on. She does not know how to modify it. She thanked the homeowner for not building another mansion and she loves the idea of a beach house; however, something is not organic about it. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Hirshorn stated that as a conceptual discussion, he does not mind the asymmetry, but believes it may be too asymmetrical with the very vertical and narrow gable and then the very wide low gable is possibly too much. One thing to consider on the porch, he has seen on similar type structures, where you can have a simple double piazza running along one side and capture some of the views that way, as opposed to the two story box type porch shown, which is awkward. Mr. Linton asked if he is suggesting to have it run the length of the house. Mr. Hirshorn responded in the affirmative. He stated that a very classic double piazza could work better if capturing the views from the second floor is the intent. That could be one idea. He stated that he does not mind the asymmetry if some of the angles were softened. Ms. Wilson stated that she definitely was not going for symmetry and agrees that she does like the asymmetry and quirkiness of it, but needs some balance where those two relate to each other better. Mr. Linton stated that their goal was to design the most efficient house possible and part of that is being a young growing family with budget constraints. He felt that each comment made added several thousand to the budget. Ms. Wilson disagreed and stated that it was really a massing discussion. She stated that Mr. Hirshorn was not increasing the size of the porch, but adjusting the proportions of it so that it felt more anchored to the house and less than something extended from the house. It was not an add, just a scale. She stated that the Commission is here to comment on scale and massing. She stated that it does not have to run the full length nor does it have to be traditional, but needs to engage the form a little better. Mr. Hirshorn stated that there are a number of examples of those two story piazzas on simpler structures both downtown Charleston and in the Old Village and is more tied into the house. He does not believe any additional money will be spent, just a different design. Mr. Linton asked if the Commission is suggesting putting a roof on it as well or is the pergola acceptable. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the pergola would be more of an extension of a porch under one of the gables as a traditional piazza would be. You would lose the openness. Mr. Linton asked about extending the gable roof. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would. Ms. Wilson asked if he means having more of a shed roof; a porch roof that ties in. She stated that she does not want to rule out the pergola, if that is a goal for the homeowner. It is about the form engaging with the house, whether it is slats or a roof is more personal than the massing that is seen from the street. She stated that waterproofing the porch is going to be difficult if the pergola is the homeowner’s decision. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan stated that he would be more in opposition with the pergola. Since he has served on the Commission, very few pergolas have been approved. He stated that he is not in favor of the pergolas. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the comment on waterproofing is significant. He stated that having a fixed roof would help tremendously, as without them they rot quickly. Ms. Wilson moved to approve as submitted, the request for demolition at 966 Pitt Street; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Keenan asked for the dimension of the existing deck. Ms. Thomas said that it is nine feet by thirteen feet. like to rotate the home so that the long side is facing the road and the short side is now the deck. tms-532-01-00-092~design~2017-07-10~0:
Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Kate Campbell, Beau Clowney Architects, stated that the house is circa 1850’s and she is doing research on the evolution. She stated that they pulled up the Sanborn maps, which show it has been added on to. She stated that the 1912 Sanborn maps show this home as a gable structure that is more of a t-shape with one story casings on the front and back, with a two-story porch. She stated that at some point the two corners were infilled and the large gable on the side elevation was put in. She said there were significant alterations to that side, but has really remained this core block of a house until the mid-1990’s when the carport structure and one story piece on the backside of the project were added. She showed illustrations to the Commission of the home. She stated that what they are proposing is to add to the rear of the structure with a link, revealing the historic corner which was obscured with the 1990’s addition, alter the kitchen area and pull it back from the main corner, alter the roof slightly, and do a one story living room addition. She stated that they are attempting to follow more preservation minded concepts. She said that landscape and paving plans were received from the owner 24 hours prior to submittal of the application, so they put it on there for reference and are still working with Sheila Wertimer’s office on what the layout will be. She stated that conceptually, she wanted to provide the framework. She stated that one of the owners is an artist and would like an art studio to paint off the living room. She added that they are not in a flood zone. She said that the side setback that they are requesting, the survey shows one corner 2.4 feet off the property line, so they will be encroaching 8.2 feet into the existing required setback. She said that they are stepping the new addition in so they are not going any further into that setback from that corner and will be about 3 feet off. Mr. Keenan stated that the middle section, where the former roof is, will be removed, that is not changing. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Campbell said that the roof will come off and the wall will move back and the other wall becomes the separation between the new kitchen and the old. She says it will feel like a link and then the new building. Batton Kennon, of Beau Clowney Architects added that Ms. Campbell mentioned that the original house has since been altered throughout the years. He stated that there was a t-shaped gable and the backside was one story up until after 1938, when it was changed. Ms. Dickson asked if they would be proposing some type of new gable. Mr. Kennon responded in the negative, as it has since been changed. He stated that the hyphen will have a new roof, because the shed will slope into the new addition. Mr. Keenan stated that it is massive, but the lot is also massive. He stated that he likes the addition and what was done with the porch, extending it out. Ms. Dickson asked if the fireplace is an inside/outside fireplace. Ms. Campbell stated that it is an outside fireplace downstairs, but not on the porch. Mr. Keenan stated that he is fine with the pool and stated that Ms. Wertimer’s landscape plan is out of the Commission’s purview. Ms. Rowe stated that she loves what has been done to take it back to what it should have been. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in reference to the proposed demolition of the addition, he would need more documentation on when it was built and that it is not historic. He stated that although it is an addition, it may still be old. Mr. Kennon stated that their research shows it was done in the mid 1990’s and any request on how this should be done, they would need some direction. Mr. Hirshorn said that how it has been accomplished in the past is documentation with slides on the interior foundations and materials so you can date it through this process. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Campbell stated that the kitchen cabinets are definitely late 1980’s to early 1990’s as well as the appliances. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would refer back to how Ms. Campbell documented the St. Andrews Church demolition of that one section from the historic structure. He stated that he would mimic this process. Mr. Keenan stated that it could also be accomplished through old surveys. Ms. Campbell stated that she could check with the Town on the permit for that time period, and she will submit this with their final request. Mr. Hirshorn stated that it looks great, but it is a substantial increase in the structure, not necessarily from the streetscape, but it is a historic structure that the applicant is proposing to add a very large new section. He added that as a precedent he is not 100% on board with such large additions to historically preserved homes. Mr. Keenan asked for the square footage of the original structure. Ms. Campbell said that the addition is approximately 480 square feet. She stated that what may be difficult to read is that there are a great deal of porches, which are open. She stated that the addition steps backs in order to be subordinate to the main structure. Mr. Keenan stated that it is deceiving on the drawings, but most of what is being added are porches. Ms. Campbell stated that it is all open underneath, as well. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he cannot recall many examples of historic houses where there has been such a large scale addition. Ms. Campbell stated that an example would be the Boatwright’s home, which was done a few years ago. She stated that this was a historic house and a two and a half story addition was added to the back side, and the lot is smaller. She said there is also the house on Morrison. Mr. Hirshorn stated that in many cases the addition mimics the historic structure, even if they are hyphenated or the gable height is lowered. He stated that in this case, an entirely new structure is being added to a historic house and he has not seen too much of this. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Campbell stated that it happens frequently downtown where there is a kitchen house that may or may not have not been connected, and there is a variation of materials, which tells a story of how something has been added on. She stated that you have the main volume of the historic piece, then a link and another building. Ms. Keenan stated that the exception for this lot is the overall size of it. He stated that the logic really applies when there is a smaller lot and a large historic home on it and then the homeowner attempts to max out the ratio. He stated that he is not aware of a lot larger than this one in the Old Village. Ms. Dickson stated that when this is complete, it will likely exceed the 50% ratio. Ms. Campbell stated that they are only at 32% impervious. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he struggles with the idea of leaving the historical structure as it is, as opposed to adding on a beautiful addition, as it does alter the historic nature of the entirety of the home and lot. He stated that from a preservation standpoint, he is unsure what the implications would be. He added that although there is room to do the addition, it is not the same house it once was. Ms. Rowe stated that it helps that the house is sitting sideways, so it is not facing the street. Mr. Hirshorn asked if the applicant could add to the application some concrete examples of where these large new additions have been added on to the back of historically preserved homes. Mr. Keenan stated that he would like to go on record to say that he really appreciates the architects’ elevations. He stated that this Commission sees all scales and believes this is a good one to use as far as what the Commission is expecting to see, especially on conceptual. He stated that it makes it much easier for the Commission.
tms-532-01-00-092~design~2017-07-10~1:
Mr. Rutherford reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Kate Campbell, architect, stated that this was before the Commission in July. She stated that they researched the Sanborn maps, and this house used to be a two story house and on the back was one story. She said at some point, they added the piece in the front and back and a large gable on the side elevation. She said what they are proposing is to demolish a portion of the kitchen and maintain the area along the side, renovate the kitchen and add a living room on the back side that is one story. She stated that they would also have a wrap-around porch on the back side opening onto the garden. She said the property is large and the homeowner would like to add to it and follow the traditional development patterns of a single house that you would see downtown or in the Old Village, where they are adding and stepping back along the length of the property. She said the homeowners are working with Sheila Wortimer on the landscape design and added some parking. She said that they are not in a flood zone so they would like to utilize the space underneath as an open area with a fireplace on the ground floor. She said that there will be a small enclosed artist studio as a portion of the porch. She said that one other thing they would like to do is change out the wood rails that are not historic and go back with a rectangular shoebox style picket with a round rail on both porches and bring it back to what is more historically appropriate. She said that the property does slope down as it goes to the rear of the property and the stair will be internal on the porch. She said they are maintaining the existing kitchen wall and not going any further into the setback and are slightly less. She said at the closest point, they are just under three feet to the property line, so this will also be a request of the Commission to allow them to continue this, because setting it in ten feet would not make sense in terms of the development on that property line. Old Village Historic District Commission

Ms. Wilson stated that the staff notes indicated that the property owners were at 40%; however, it appears they are only at 30%. She said they are well under the lot coverage. She said she appreciates that the stairs are enclosed and believes the plans look great. She asked if the columns are also going to be improved when the pickets are replaced. Ms. Campbell added that the property owners want to do a historically sensitive porch renovation. Mr. Hirshorn asked how many additional feet of encroachment is on the new addition. Ms. Campbell stated that it is approximately 33 additional feet along the length. Ross Evans, 430 Church Street next door, said the only concern he has is on the additional 33 feet. He said that this house is right on the property line and his driveway goes right next to it and when it rains, they get water. He said with the 30 additional feet, what is the property owner going to do to drain water off of the roof and where will it go. He said they currently get water and with the additional 30 feet of house, where will the water go, other than in his yard. Mr. Rutherford stated that drainage is not in the purview of the Commission and would be handled with the Town’s Building Permit division. Mr. Keenan stated that this is an accurate statement; however, it is a good question. He said that both the applicant and architect are both present. Ms. Campbell said that they would gutter that side and try to mitigate that roof slope coming off on Mr. Evan’s side. She said that they are not legally allowed to drain on any other property, but will work with Mr. Evans and their client on this. Mr. Evans stated that this would normally not be an issue; however, they have a basement that previously did not get water and when 424 Church street was renovated, they began getting water in their basement. He said that they also said they would try to keep the water off his property, but now they get water in the basement. He said when 424 Church did their renovations and built an addition on, it is 10 feet away from his home and now drains into his yard. He said he met the homeowner of 436 Church Old Village Historic District Commission

Street and does not want to create issues, but wants to know where the water will go. Ms. Wilson said that when you look at the roof plan, not a tremendous amount of the roof pitches towards Mr. Evans home and could be handled with gutters and French drains along the side of the property. Mr. Evans stated that there are gutters on the front portion of the home, but they drain into his yard. Ms. Campbell said that they will need to change the direction of the gutters. She said they could do a sub-surface pipe that the gutters tie into that will stay on the property. She said they can explore ways to mitigate, but attempting to control it with gutters would be the most effective. Mr. Keenan said that all this Commission is able to do is ask that the architect and landscape planner work with Mr. Evans to come up with a plan that is adequate. He said that both the architect and landscape planners are reputable. He asked Ms. Campbell to continue the communication with Mr. Evans and advise Ms. Wortimer that there is some concern as well. Mr. Hirshorn stated that he would reiterate for the record that with an additional 30 feet of encroachment, the Commission would like to make certain that those stipulations are followed through. He said that this is an extensive amount of additional encroachment and realizes that they are allowed to follow the house line, which is already encroaching on the property line. He said that this is a large amount of addition and the water will go somewhere, and although there are ways to mitigate this to some extent, the likelihood is that there will be some runoff. He said he would like to make sure that there is follow through and everything is handled satisfactorily. Ms. Rowe stated that they are doing the historic portion of the house a huge favor and taking it back to what it looked like with integrity. Mr. Keenan said that he would like to reiterate Mr. Hirshorn’s concerns and added that every month, this Commission has drainage issues that arise in these meetings and technically it is not in the Commission’s purview; however, wishes that the Commission did have some input in this regard. He said that it is up to individual property owners to be good stewards and Old Village Historic District Commission

be considerate of their neighbors. He said that the project as a whole, looks good. Ms. Rowe made a motion to accept the application for final review for 436 Church Street as presented; seconded by Ms. Dickson. All present voted in favor.

Mr. Pohlman reviewed staff comments with the Commission. Scott Broadwell, homeowner stated that he is here with this father, Russ Broadwell. He stated that they received a lot of positive feedback in March when they presented and at that time, the design was enclosure of the carport and an “L” shaped addition on the back. He stated that the application indicates a two story addition; however, it is a one and a half story addition. He stated that the upper level has a five foot knee wall. He illustrated the street rendering of what the street level would look like with the addition in the back with the enclosure of the carport. He stated that there is mention of demolition and what is being demolished is a small section, which is an unheated laundry room. He stated that they were able to preserve the porch and the craftsman look of the porch. He stated that looking from the front, there are two Old Village Historic District Commission

bays that are open and one will be enclosed. He stated that they are extended slightly back from that and making it into an L shape. He stated that the porch in the back is open. He stated that they reduced the scale from the March conceptual and will maintain the historic corner on the house. He reviewed with the Commission the two side elevations. Mr. Hirshorn stated that his only initial question is if the proposed demolition of the old laundry room section is historic. Mr. Broadwell stated that it is built on cinder block with separate materials from the original structure. He stated that it was the most recent addition to the property; however, they do not have anything in the permitting office that is able to date this. He stated that it was built with non-historic components. Mr. Hirshorn asked if there is an illustration of that area on an existing elevation. Mr. Broadwell stated that the structure went through several different evolutions and looking at the types of material in the piers, and the original structure was a Fisherman’s cottage and the front gable structure was then brought out as the second element and the third element was what enclosed the front porch and created the carport and then the last evolution was the added laundry room. He stated that it is constructed of different materials, has different siding and piers, and is not heated. Mr. Hirshorn asked Mr. Broadwell what year he believes this was added. Mr. Broadwell stated that based on the materials, he would estimate the 1970’s. He stated that the flooring is 1970’s Formica and it has butylene plumbing. Mr. Keenan asked if this would be the only section demolished. Mr. Broadwell stated that when they presented in March for conceptual review, this was the same component discussed that the Commission indicated was acceptable. Mr. Keenan asked if the pool was added. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Broadwell stated that this was not present in March and said that it is a plunge pool for his children and is not visible from the street. Mr. Keenan stated that he knows the homeowner has been working very hard on this project and he appreciates the effort. He said that he likes the design in the front, the enclosure on the carport, but a little nervous about the height in the back and hopes conceptually, that it does not dwarfing the historic structure. Mr. Broadwell stated that the flood code requires them to come up sixteen inches, so the front of the house obscures more of the back by coming up slightly. He stated that the total height is just under 26 feet and well within regulation. He stated that it is shorter than the one that was presented in March, coming down two feet. Colin Cope, with Heather Wilson office, stated that this is next to Heather Wilson’s home and this is a very familiar situation where you have a small cottage on the front and slightly pushed back from the street and then there is a small section, they refer to as hyphens to the one and a half story. He stated that when you are in the front of Ms. Wilson’s house, you do not even know the other structure is back there and it is larger than Mr. Broadwell’s. Ms. Rowe stated that the homeowner has done a remarkable job and loves what was accomplished in the front. Mr. Hirshorn stated that where the new addition is there is not a big height differential; however, from another angle, the roof is much lower. Mr. Broadwell stated that it does not build perspective whereas the other angle does. He stated that from the street, the lower part of the windows are obscured. He said from the street, the lower half of the window should not be visible. Mr. Cope explained the different perspectives and added that the tree shown is massive. He stated that you are not able to see the new structure, because of the tree. He stated that it leans out over the house in between the carport and what is being shown in the back. Old Village Historic District Commission

Mr. Keenan asked what the total square footage of the proposed addition. Mr. Broadwell stated that it is 2,500 total square feet. Mr. Keenan stated that he looking for the square footage of the addition. Mr. Hirshorn stated that the addition is 1,100 square feet. Mr. Keenan stated that it is a challenging lot and believes that it looks very good. Ms. Rowe stated that they have done a great job keeping the Craftsman look together. Mr. Cope said that what they are doing is filling in a carport which are not traditional and filling it in will provide a more traditional look. Ms. Dickson stated that it is a shame to take a small house and put a large addition in the back. She stated that she does; however, likes it much better than the initial design, because the character of the Fisherman’s Cottage was kept. Mr. Broadwell stated that they attempted to try and do the addition as discreetly and appropriately as possible without losing the character. Ms. Dickson asked how far the pool was from the lot line. Mr. Colin stated that it is currently just a placeholder and could be moved around. Mr. Keenan stated that the application does not include the pool. He stated that the Commission is addressing the house. Mr. Hirshorn stated that unfortunately he was not at the conceptual meeting; however, if he had been there, he would have recommended creating the square footage that is less visible from the street. He stated that this is his only reservation. He stated that when these additions are added on to historic structures, at what point is preservation being compromised and how important is this. He said that this is clearly visible from the street and alters the streetscape of a historical structure. He stated that he does not have an issue with demolishing the Old Village Historic District Commission

utility room; however the streetscape of a historic structure is being altered. Mr. Broadwell stated that since the March conceptual, they have scaled back the size and height considerably. He stated that the structure has already gone through several evolutions and this is just part of the evolution. He stated that this helps this structure evolve in to the future and hope this is the last evolution. Mr. Keenan stated that there are not many of these Fisherman’s cottages left and all that can be done is to be good stewards and protect historical structures. Mr. Hirshorn asked if any other one story designs were considered. Mr. Broadwell stated that it would encroach on the rear neighbor, which was not acceptable to the Commission. Mr. Hirshorn asked what the grounds were for the demolition for the utility section. Mr. Broadwell stated that the concrete block would not be able to support the new addition. Mr. Cope stated that that he would certainly say A, which is poor construction and obviously has safety issues. Mr. Broadwell stated that he would select “A” for demolition. Mr. Hirshorn made a motion to approve the demolition of the utility shed section to the rear of the property based on guideline “A” under partial demolition of historic structures, public safety; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor. Ms. Rowe made a motion to approve the application for 728 Pitt Street, final review for additions and alterations; seconded by Mr. Hirshorn. All present voted in favor. III. Staff Approvals Mr. Pohlman stated that there were no staff approvals. Old Village Historic District Commission

VI. Motion to Adjourn Ms. Dickson motioned to adjourn; seconded by Ms. Rowe. All present voted in favor. There being no further business, meeting adjourned at 7:06 p.m.

Respectfully submitted, Barbara Ashe
